伯主無恤患之誠，《春秋》嚴誅心之法。此齊桓之兩救邢，始以人，繼而次，同一伯者不誠之心也。《春秋》得不原其心而誅之也哉？世入春秋，王靈不振，中夏之統莫属，外夷之患荐興，人心所賴以維持者，伯也。乃今齊桓主伯，宅心安攘，始因狄為邢患而救之也，既遣一軍以往；繼因邢被狄難而恤之也，又率三國偕行。拯恤之念有在，簡書之義以伸，聖人於此宜有美詞稱揚其績
translation_en:
…among those of low station. Had Duke Zhuang recognized and employed him early, with such a man serving the state, Qi would surely have abandoned its designs. Why go to the trouble of dredging the Zhu River? Why come to battle? Earlier Confucian scholars called Duke Zhuang a ruler without resolve who could establish nothing. How true!
“The men of Qi relieved Xing.” 〔First year of Duke Min.〕 “The armies of Qi, Song, and Cao encamped at Niebei to relieve Xing.” 〔First year of Duke Xi.〕
Mo Pu
Comment by Associate Examiner Xia, Instructor: 〔Those who write on this topic often base their argument on insufficient effort and lack of courage. They grasp the point, but have not refined their understanding. This essay probes the subtleties of the hegemon’s motives. Its language and tone are concise and rigorous, sweeping away the defects of stale formulations. Selected for inclusion.〕
Comment by Examiner Chen, School Instructor: 〔The handling of the wording is careful and rigorous.〕
Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: 〔It grasps the sage’s method of condemning motives through his brush.〕
When a hegemonic lord lacks sincerity in relieving distress, the Spring and Autumn Annals rigorously applies its method of condemning motives. Thus, in Duke Huan of Qi’s two attempts to relieve Xing, the first entry calls his force “men,” while the second records that it “encamped”: both disclose the same insincerity in the hegemon’s heart. Could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to examine his motives and condemn him?
As the world entered the Spring and Autumn period, royal authority languished, no one held unified command over the central states, and troubles from foreign peoples repeatedly arose. It was upon hegemons that people relied to sustain order. Now Duke Huan of Qi assumed the hegemony, setting his mind on securing the central states and repelling outsiders. First, when the Di brought trouble upon Xing, he sent an army to its relief. Later, when Xing suffered disaster at the hands of the Di, he again came to its aid, leading the forces of three states together. His intention to rescue and relieve was evident, and the duty enjoined by the written summons was fulfilled. Here, surely, the sage ought to have used words of praise to extol his achievements…

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而責其不誠何耶盖救欲盡力不力不誠也救
欲速徃不速亦不誠也桓公始之救也聊遣一
軍而大衆不行力不盡矣継之救也雖合三師
而聶北有次徃不速矣桓亦何如其心哉吾知
桓之心以為邢患未甚而弭之則在彼感德之
心不深狄虐未甚而撲之則在我恤患之名不
顯將隆其名必張其功将張其功必養其患養
患之心生則救患分災之義泯要功之念作則
玩寇待弊之志形是以師出而苟簡不力者由
===
此師行而逗留不進者由此卒使狄鋒莫遏邢
都遂遷是果誰之責耶皆桓公始謀匪臧一念
不誠所致也春秋得不責之哉故其始之救邢
特書曰人終之救邢特書曰次而桓公不力不
速之所以咸凛然於筆削之下矣誅心之法何
其嚴哉雖然桓公救邢之責固難逃矣然邢遷
之後為之築城郭以防其患具器用以賙其乏
使邢之君臣無國而有國又誰之功耶說者謂
其得興滅継絕之義而謂二百四十二年之美
punctuated: 而責其不誠，何耶？盖救欲盡力，不力，不誠也；救欲速徃，不速，亦不誠也。桓公始之救也，聊遣一軍而大衆不行，力不盡矣；継之救也，雖合三師而聶北有次，徃不速矣。桓亦何如其心哉？吾知桓之心以為：邢患未甚而弭之，則在彼感德之心不深；狄虐未甚而撲之，則在我恤患之名不顯。將隆其名，必張其功；将張其功，必養其患。養患之心生，則救患分災之義泯；要功之念作，則玩寇待弊之志形。是以師出而苟簡不力者由此，師行而逗留不進者由此。卒使狄鋒莫遏，邢都遂遷，是果誰之責耶？皆桓公始謀匪臧、一念不誠所致也。《春秋》得不責之哉？故其始之救邢，特書曰「人」；終之救邢，特書曰「次」。而桓公不力不速之所以，咸凛然於筆削之下矣。誅心之法，何其嚴哉！雖然，桓公救邢之責固難逃矣，然邢遷之後，為之築城郭以防其患，具器用以賙其乏，使邢之君臣無國而有國，又誰之功耶？說者謂其得興滅継絕之義，而謂二百四十二年之美
translation_en:
…yet why does it reproach him for his insincerity? Aid requires exerting one's full strength; failure to do so is insincerity. Aid requires going swiftly; failure to do so is also insincerity. When Duke Huan first went to Xing's rescue, he merely dispatched one army without mobilizing his main forces: he did not exert his full strength. When he subsequently came to its rescue, although he assembled the armies of three states, he halted at Niebei: he did not advance swiftly. What, then, was in Huan's heart? I understand his thinking to have been this: if Xing's troubles were quelled before they became severe, its gratitude for his kindness would not be deep; if the Di's depredations were suppressed before they became severe, his own reputation for relieving distress would not be conspicuous. To magnify his reputation, he had to magnify his achievements; to magnify his achievements, he had to nurture the calamity. Once the desire to nurture calamity arose, the righteous purpose of relieving distress and sharing the burden of disaster vanished. Once the thought of claiming credit arose, the intention to treat the enemy lightly and await Xing's exhaustion took shape. This explains why his troops set out with careless half-measures and insufficient effort; this explains why, once on the march, they lingered and failed to advance. In the end, the Di's onslaught went unchecked, and Xing's capital consequently had to be moved. Whose responsibility was this, indeed? It all resulted from Duke Huan's unsound initial design and a single insincere thought. Could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to reproach him? Thus, for his first rescue of Xing, it deliberately writes “men”; for his final rescue of Xing, it deliberately writes “encamped.” The motives behind Duke Huan's failure to exert himself and to act swiftly are thereby all laid bare beneath the stern judgment of its editorial brush. How rigorous is its principle of condemning intentions!

Nevertheless, although Duke Huan certainly cannot escape blame for his rescue of Xing, after Xing relocated, he built its inner and outer walls to protect it from danger and supplied implements and necessities to relieve its shortages. He enabled Xing's ruler and ministers, who had lost their state, to possess a state once more. Whose achievement, in turn, was this? Commentators say that he fulfilled the righteous purpose of restoring extinguished states and continuing severed lines of succession, and call it an admirable deed of the two hundred and forty-two years…

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
事有方叔城東方南仲城朔方遺意良有以夫
禮記
次國之卿命於其君者如小國之卿天子之
大夫為三監監於諸侯之國者其祿視諸
侯之卿
陳雍
同考試官教諭崔批王制一題重在制祿諸作詳畧失宜甚至有不知祿數者晚陳此卷簡潔明快必究心於經本者健羡健羡
考試官學正陳批說出尊王重内之意可嘉
===
考試官教授黃批得先王制祿之意允宜錄之
外臣命於主君者祿既有所視王臣監於侯國
者祿亦有所視夫先王班祿各適其宜也然外
臣命於主君者祿既如小國之卿矣則王臣監
於侯國者其祿得不視諸侯之卿哉記王制者
重釋篇首言制祿之意謂夫先王班祿之制必
因事而適變通之宜彼諸伯之三卿有命於天
子者焉有命於主君者焉命於天子者授以三
大夫之祿矣命於主君者其祿若同於天子之
punctuated:
事，有方叔城東方、南仲城朔方遺意，良有以夫！
禮記
次國之卿命於其君者，如小國之卿。天子之大夫為三監，監於諸侯之國者，其祿視諸侯之卿。
陳雍
同考試官教諭崔批：王制一題，重在制祿。諸作詳畧失宜，甚至有不知祿數者。晚陳此卷，簡潔明快，必究心於經本者。健羡！健羡！
考試官學正陳批：說出尊王重内之意，可嘉。
考試官教授黃批：得先王制祿之意，允宜錄之。
外臣命於主君者，祿既有所視；王臣監於侯國者，祿亦有所視。夫先王班祿，各適其宜也。然外臣命於主君者，祿既如小國之卿矣，則王臣監於侯國者，其祿得不視諸侯之卿哉？記王制者，重釋篇首言制祿之意，謂夫先王班祿之制，必因事而適變通之宜。彼諸伯之三卿，有命於天子者焉，有命於主君者焉。命於天子者，授以三大夫之祿矣。命於主君者，其祿若同於天子之
translation_en:
…deeds, preserving something of the spirit of Fang Shu’s fortification of the eastern regions and Nan Zhong’s fortification of Shuofang—there is indeed good reason for this judgment!

Book of Rites

“Ministers of a medium-sized state appointed by their own ruler receive stipends like those of ministers of a small state. Grand masters of the Son of Heaven who serve as the Three Supervisors, overseeing the states of the feudal lords, receive stipends equivalent to those of the feudal lords’ ministers.”

Chen Yong

Comment by Associate Examiner Cui, School Instructor: “The question on ‘Royal Regulations’ centers on the regulation of stipends. The other compositions are ill-judged in their proportions of detail and brevity; some writers do not even know the amounts of the stipends. This paper, presented late [?], is concise, clear, and brisk. Its author must have carefully studied the text of the Classic. Admirable! Admirable! [?]”

Comment by Examiner Chen, School Instructor: “It brings out the intention of honoring the king and giving greater weight to the central court. Commendable.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “It grasps the intention behind the former kings’ regulation of stipends. It certainly deserves selection.”

For officials outside the royal court appointed by their own ruler, there is an established standard for their stipends; for royal officials supervising the feudal states, there is likewise an established standard. The former kings apportioned stipends as was appropriate to each case. Now, if officials outside the royal court appointed by their own ruler receive stipends like those of ministers of a small state, should not royal officials supervising the feudal states receive stipends equivalent to those of the feudal lords’ ministers?

The recorder of ‘Royal Regulations’ further explains the intention behind the discussion of stipends at the beginning of the chapter: the former kings’ system for apportioning stipends necessarily accommodated circumstances and made appropriate adjustments. Of the three ministers serving each earl, some were appointed by the Son of Heaven and others by their own ruler. Those appointed by the Son of Heaven were granted the stipends of the three grand masters. If those appointed by their own ruler received the same stipends as those appointed by the Son of Heaven …

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所命則君臣之分不幾於無别乎故必如小國
之卿于以受田一千六百畝計其所入可食一
百四十四人焉所以然者以諸伯所命降於天
子之所命故也若夫天子之大夫有在朝守常
職者焉有使外為三監者焉守常職者授以視
子男之田矣監於侯國者其禄若等於諸侯之
大夫則内外之分不幾於無辨乎故必視大國
之卿于以受田三千二百畝計其所入可食二
百八十八人焉所以然者以王朝之臣尊於諸
===
侯之大夫故也噫一班禄之間尊王重内其制
有如是夫抑論之分田制禄王政之首務故此
篇自天子之田方千里至制農田百畝乃其經
制之常法此之所言又其變通之異宜於常法
之中而有變通者存則先王經制大備巨細畢
舉此亦可見其一端云有天下者鑒諸
致樂以治心則易直子諒之心油然生矣易
直子諒之心生則樂樂則安安則久久則
天天則神天則不言而信神則不怒而威
punctuated:
所命，則君臣之分不幾於無别乎？故必如小國之卿，于以受田一千六百畝，計其所入，可食一百四十四人焉。所以然者，以諸伯所命降於天子之所命故也。若夫天子之大夫，有在朝守常職者焉，有使外為三監者焉。守常職者，授以視子男之田矣；監於侯國者，其禄若等於諸侯之大夫，則内外之分不幾於無辨乎？故必視大國之卿，于以受田三千二百畝，計其所入，可食二百八十八人焉。所以然者，以王朝之臣尊於諸侯之大夫故也。噫！一班禄之間，尊王重内，其制有如是夫！抑論之，分田制禄，王政之首務。故此篇自天子之田方千里，至制農田百畝，乃其經制之常法；此之所言，又其變通之異宜。於常法之中而有變通者存，則先王經制大備，巨細畢舉。此亦可見其一端云。有天下者鑒諸！

致樂以治心，則易直子諒之心油然生矣。易直子諒之心生則樂，樂則安，安則久，久則天，天則神。天則不言而信，神則不怒而威。
translation_en:
…those appointed by the Son of Heaven, would the distinction between ruler and subject not come close to disappearing? Their emoluments must therefore equal those of a minister of a small state: they receive 1,600 mu of land, whose yield, reckoned in provisions, can feed 144 people. This is because those appointed by the earls rank below those appointed by the Son of Heaven. As for the Son of Heaven’s grand masters, some remain at court to discharge regular duties, while others are sent abroad to serve as the Three Supervisors. Those discharging regular duties are granted land on a scale corresponding to that of viscounts and barons. If those supervising the feudal states received emoluments equal to those of the feudal lords’ grand masters, would the distinction between the central court and the outer states not come close to disappearing? Their emoluments must therefore correspond to those of a minister of a large state: they receive 3,200 mu of land, whose yield, reckoned in provisions, can feed 288 people. This is because ministers of the royal court are more exalted than the feudal lords’ grand masters. Ah! Even in the apportionment of emoluments, such were the institutions for honoring the king and giving precedence to the central court! Moreover, allocating land and regulating emoluments are the foremost tasks of kingly government. Thus, this chapter, from its provision that the Son of Heaven’s domain measures a thousand li square to its prescription of a hundred mu of farmland, sets out the standing rules of the institutional order. What is discussed here concerns the particular adjustments appropriate to changing circumstances. Since provision for adaptation exists within the standing rules, the former kings’ institutions were fully comprehensive, attending to matters great and small alike. Here, too, one can glimpse an aspect of that achievement. Let those who possess All-under-Heaven take heed!

When music is brought to its fullest realization to govern the heart, a disposition of ease, uprightness, kindness, and sincerity arises spontaneously. When such a disposition arises, there is joy; joy brings repose; repose brings constancy; constancy brings accord with Heaven; accord with Heaven brings spiritual efficacy. In accord with Heaven, one is trusted without speaking; through spiritual efficacy, one inspires awe without anger…

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
致樂以治心者也致禮以治躬則莊敬莊
敬則嚴威心中斯須不和不樂而鄙詐之
心入之矣外貌斯須不莊不敬而易慢之
心入之矣故樂也者動於内者也禮也者
動於外者也
鄭文標
同考試官教諭批此題經註明白只余體認不真往往
失旨此篇見理精到措詞典雅殆治身心有得者歟一薦何忝
考試官學正陳批納繁就簡辭理俱到録之
考試官教授黄批辭能說理其達禮樂之體用矣可取
窮禮樂以治心身者有其驗原禮樂能治心身
者有其由甚矣禮樂之切於人也兹欲心身各
得其治而有其驗舎禮樂其何以哉記者論禮
樂不可斯須去身及此謂夫樂所以窮本知變
而治心莫切焉君子研窮其理以治心則邪穢
以滌而易直慈良之心油然生矣善端以萌而
欣喜愛樂之情勃然興矣樂則從容而安何勉
強焉安則不息而久何間斷焉久則渾然天成
punctuated:
致樂以治心者也。致禮以治躬，則莊敬；莊敬則嚴威。心中斯須不和不樂，而鄙詐之心入之矣；外貌斯須不莊不敬，而易慢之心入之矣。故樂也者，動於内者也；禮也者，動於外者也。

鄭文標

同考試官教諭批：此題經註明白，只余體認不真，往往失旨。此篇見理精到，措詞典雅，殆治身心有得者歟！一薦何忝？
考試官學正陳批：納繁就簡，辭理俱到，録之。
考試官教授黄批：辭能說理，其達禮樂之體用矣，可取。

窮禮樂以治心身者，有其驗；原禮樂能治心身者，有其由。甚矣，禮樂之切於人也！兹欲心身各得其治而有其驗，舎禮樂，其何以哉？記者論禮樂不可斯須去身，及此謂夫樂所以窮本知變，而治心莫切焉。君子研窮其理以治心，則邪穢以滌，而易直慈良之心油然生矣；善端以萌，而欣喜愛樂之情勃然興矣。樂則從容而安，何勉強焉？安則不息而久，何間斷焉？久則渾然天成
translation_en:
…This is what it means to bring music to its fullest realization in order to govern the mind. Bringing ritual to its fullest realization in order to regulate one’s person produces gravity and reverence; gravity and reverence produce dignity and authority. If the mind lacks harmony and joy for even a moment, baseness and deceit enter it. If the outward bearing lacks gravity and reverence for even a moment, carelessness and arrogance enter the mind. Thus music acts within, while ritual acts without.

Zheng Wenbiao

Comment by the Associate Examiner, an Instructor: “The canonical text and commentary for this topic are clear; it is merely that apprehension of them is not genuine [?], so writers often miss their purport. This essay’s understanding of principle is penetrating and precise, and its wording refined and elegant. Might its author have attained something through the cultivation of his person and mind? What could be unworthy about recommending him?”
Comment by Examiner Chen, a School Director: “He brings complexity into a concise compass, doing full justice to both expression and principle. Select it.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, a Prefectural School Professor: “His language can elucidate principle. He has surely comprehended the substance and function of ritual and music. Worth selecting.”

When one thoroughly explores ritual and music to govern the mind and person, there are demonstrable results; when one investigates how ritual and music can govern the mind and person, there are underlying reasons. How profoundly ritual and music concern human beings! If we now wish both mind and person to be properly governed, with demonstrable results, by what means could we accomplish this if we abandoned ritual and music? The author of the Record, discussing why ritual and music cannot be separated from one’s person for even a moment, reaches this point and explains that music is the means of fathoming the root and understanding change, and nothing bears more directly on governing the mind. When the gentleman thoroughly investigates its principles in order to govern his mind, perversity and impurity are washed away, and a disposition of ease, uprightness, kindness, and goodness spontaneously arises. The beginnings of goodness sprout, and feelings of delight, affection, and joy vigorously emerge. Joy brings composure and repose: what forced effort is there? Repose brings unceasing endurance: what interruption is there? Endurance brings an integral, natural perfection…

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不假作為也天則變化無方不可度思也天雖
何言而人自信之如蓍龜神雖不怒而人自威
之如鈇鉞致樂治心之驗如此則窮本知變之
妙可以盡識矣禮所以著誠去偽而治躬莫要
焉君子研窮其理以治躬則足以固肌膚之會
而莊敬之容儼乎其可掬矣夫既莊敬則足以
著恭肅之儀而嚴威之象凛乎其難犯矣斯時
也心中宜無斯須之不和樂也使有或間則鄙
詐之心寧不乘間而入乎外貌宜無斯須之不
===
莊敬也使有或息則易慢之心寧不抵隙而
乎致禮治躬之驗如此則著誠去偽之心不可
少間矣然樂之所以能治心者非有他也蓋樂
由中出動於内者也動於内則能治心而極其
和焉禮之所以能治躬者非無自也蓋禮自外
作動於外者也動於外則能治躬而極其順焉
吁禮樂之切於心身如此夫豈可斯須去耶雖
然禮樂之功用非特治心治躬而已觀之下文
曰樂極和禮極順以至德輝動於内而民莫不
punctuated: 不假作為也。天則變化無方，不可度思也。天雖何言，而人自信之如蓍龜；神雖不怒，而人自威之如鈇鉞。致樂治心之驗如此，則窮本知變之妙可以盡識矣。禮所以著誠去偽，而治躬莫要焉。君子研窮其理以治躬，則足以固肌膚之會，而莊敬之容儼乎其可掬矣。夫既莊敬，則足以著恭肅之儀，而嚴威之象凛乎其難犯矣。斯時也，心中宜無斯須之不和樂也。使有或間，則鄙詐之心寧不乘間而入乎？外貌宜無斯須之不莊敬也。使有或息，則易慢之心寧不抵隙而乎？致禮治躬之驗如此，則著誠去偽之心不可少間矣。然樂之所以能治心者，非有他也，蓋樂由中出，動於内者也。動於内，則能治心而極其和焉。禮之所以能治躬者，非無自也，蓋禮自外作，動於外者也。動於外，則能治躬而極其順焉。吁！禮樂之切於心身如此，夫豈可斯須去耶？雖然，禮樂之功用非特治心治躬而已。觀之下文曰：「樂極和，禮極順。」以至「德輝動於内，而民莫不
translation_en: …without depending on deliberate effort. When it accords with Heaven, its transformations have no fixed pattern and cannot be fathomed by thought. Though Heaven says nothing, people naturally trust it as they do milfoil stalks and tortoise shells used in divination; though the numinous displays no anger, people naturally stand in awe of it as they do executioners’ axes. Such are the demonstrable effects of bringing music to its fullest realization to govern the heart; from these one may fully comprehend the subtle efficacy of probing origins and understanding change. Ritual makes sincerity manifest and eliminates falsity; nothing is more essential to governing one’s person. When the gentleman thoroughly investigates its principles to govern his person, he can bring firmness to the bodily frame, and his solemn, reverent bearing becomes plainly perceptible. Once he is solemn and reverent, he can manifest a respectful and dignified deportment, and his stern, awe-inspiring appearance commands such respect that it is difficult to affront him. In this state, his heart should never lack harmony and joy, even for an instant. Should there be any interruption, would base and deceitful thoughts not seize the opening and enter? His outward appearance should never lack solemnity and reverence, even for an instant. Should these ever cease, would thoughts of carelessness and arrogance not exploit the gap [?]? Such are the demonstrable effects of bringing ritual to its fullest realization to govern one’s person; thus the intention to manifest sincerity and eliminate falsity must not lapse even briefly. text:
承聰理發諸外而民莫不承順感人動物其效
如此君子極致禮樂之道雖舉而措之天下無
難矣治心云乎哉治躬云乎哉讀者不可不知

帝王所傳心法之要
周澤

===
考試官學正陳批論以識見遠大立說而文足以
之作手也起敬起敬
考試官教授黃批論超衆作高為無疑
論曰帝王識見遠大斯有以遍天下及後
世也蓋識見近小者則為事業也促狹立
根本也淺易垂統緒也不久如器不宏所
受不多如水無源其涸可待必然之理也
有為博厚載物之事業立深固不拔之根
本垂悠久無窮之統緒蓋必識見度越為
punctuated:
承，聰理發諸外，而民莫不承順。感人動物，其效如此，君子極致禮樂之道，雖舉而措之天下，無難矣。治心云乎哉？治躬云乎哉？讀者不可不知。

帝王所傳心法之要

When the gentleman brings the Way of ritual and music to its fullest realization, he can readily apply it throughout the world. Can this be spoken of merely as ordering the heart? title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
天地立心為生民立命為萬世開太平者
之所能也知此則南軒張氏有謂帝王所
傳心法之要思過半矣請繹厥旨漢光知
竇融之計人以為明見萬里矣而吾所謂
帝王識見之遠者則不在是宋祖以三河
為帶人以為氣象不小矣而吾所謂帝王
識見之大者亦不在是然則帝王識見遠
大者何在重農是也農事何謂稼穡織紝
是也或者謂有大人之事有小人之事
===
以人君之尊而屑屑於農夫稼穡之事似
非急務君臨外朝后總內政以王后之貴
而瑣瑣於農婦織紝之事似昧大體噫帝
王之重農事非謂與民並耕而後食也抑
非吾身自織而後衣也其識其見盖謂治
常生於克敬而亂常生於驕肆誠使為國
者每念乎稼穡之勞而其后妃又不忘乎
織紝之事則心有不存焉者寡矣心既常
存必嚴恭朝夕而不敢怠也必懷保小民
punctuated: 天地立心，為生民立命，為萬世開太平者之所能也。知此，則南軒張氏有謂帝王所傳心法之要，思過半矣。請繹厥旨。漢光知竇融之計，人以為明見萬里矣，而吾所謂帝王識見之遠者，則不在是。宋祖以三河為帶，人以為氣象不小矣，而吾所謂帝王識見之大者，亦不在是。然則帝王識見遠大者何在？重農是也。農事何謂？稼穡織紝是也。或者謂：「有大人之事，有小人之事。以人君之尊，而屑屑於農夫稼穡之事，似非急務；君臨外朝，后總內政，以王后之貴，而瑣瑣於農婦織紝之事，似昧大體。」噫！帝王之重農事，非謂與民並耕而後食也，抑非吾身自織而後衣也。其識其見，盖謂治常生於克敬，而亂常生於驕肆。誠使為國者每念乎稼穡之勞，而其后妃又不忘乎織紝之事，則心有不存焉者寡矣。心既常存，必嚴恭朝夕而不敢怠也，必懷保小民
translation_en:
…to establish a mind for Heaven and Earth, establish a livelihood for the people, and inaugurate enduring peace for ten thousand generations: these are achievements within the capacity of such men. Understanding this takes us more than halfway toward grasping what Master Zhang of Nanxuan called the essentials of the method of cultivating the mind transmitted by emperors and kings. Let me unfold its meaning. Emperor Guangwu of Han understood Dou Rong’s plans, and people considered his insight capable of reaching ten thousand li. Yet this is not what I mean by the far-reaching discernment of emperors and kings. The founding emperor of Song regarded the Sanhe region as his girdle, and people considered his vision far from small. Yet this, too, is not what I mean by the breadth of imperial and royal discernment. Where, then, does such far-reaching and broad discernment lie? In valuing agriculture. What is meant by agricultural work? Sowing and harvesting, weaving and working thread.

Some might say: “There are the tasks of great men and the tasks of lesser men. For someone with the dignity of a ruler to busy himself with a farmer’s sowing and harvesting seems hardly an urgent duty. The ruler presides over the outer court, and the queen oversees the inner administration. For someone with the queen’s exalted status to concern herself with the minutiae of farm women’s weaving seems to betray ignorance of the larger principles.” Ah! When emperors and kings value agricultural work, this does not mean that they must plow alongside the people before they eat, nor that they must weave their own cloth before they dress. Their understanding and discernment rest, rather, on the recognition that order regularly arises from maintaining reverence, while disorder regularly arises from arrogance and self-indulgence. If those who govern a state truly keep in mind the toil of sowing and harvesting, and their queens and consorts likewise do not forget the work of weaving, then seldom will they fail to preserve their moral awareness. Once this awareness is constantly preserved, they will assuredly remain solemn and reverent morning and evening, never daring to be negligent; they will assuredly cherish and protect the common people…

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而不敢康也必思天下之飢猶已飢之必
思天下之寒猶已寒之土木之功不興邊
鄙之釁不開不興不開慮有以妨天下之
農事也服飾之用不僭錦綺之施不濫不
僭不濫慮有以害天下之女工也一農事
之妨所繫若不重也天下不農吾何以食
一女工之害所關若不大也天下不蠶吾
曷以衣帝王之識之見其遠也在此其大
也在此是以聲名洋溢於中國恩澤普及
===
於八荒事功廣博而深厚也措天下如泰
山之安置四海如盤石之固根本深固而
不搖也創業於前垂統於後一世肯堂肯
構則一世安富尊榮享之為不盡也百世
不愆不忘則百世祿位名壽用之豈有窮
乎以至於千世萬世莫不皆然是豈不重
農事而任權謀術數者能為如此之事業
乎能立如此之根本乎能垂如此之統緒
乎所以古之帝王以禮樂刑政為治世之
punctuated: 而不敢康也，必思天下之飢猶已飢之，必思天下之寒猶已寒之。土木之功不興，邊鄙之釁不開；不興不開，慮有以妨天下之農事也。服飾之用不僭，錦綺之施不濫；不僭不濫，慮有以害天下之女工也。一農事之妨，所繫若不重也；天下不農，吾何以食？一女工之害，所關若不大也；天下不蠶，吾曷以衣？帝王之識之見，其遠也在此，其大也在此。是以聲名洋溢於中國，恩澤普及於八荒，事功廣博而深厚也。措天下如泰山之安，置四海如盤石之固，根本深固而不搖也。創業於前，垂統於後，一世肯堂肯構，則一世安富尊榮，享之為不盡也；百世不愆不忘，則百世祿位名壽，用之豈有窮乎？以至於千世萬世，莫不皆然。是豈不重農事而任權謀術數者，能為如此之事業乎？能立如此之根本乎？能垂如此之統緒乎？所以古之帝王以禮樂刑政為治世之
translation_en:
…and would not dare indulge in ease. They would surely regard the hunger of all under Heaven as though they themselves had caused it, and the cold suffered by all under Heaven as though they themselves had caused it. They would undertake no construction projects and provoke no conflicts on the frontiers, fearing that these might obstruct farming throughout the realm. They would not exceed the prescribed bounds in their use of clothing and ornaments, nor lavishly employ brocades and patterned silks, fearing that these might impair women’s textile work throughout the realm. An impediment to a single farming task may seem of little consequence; yet if no one under Heaven farms, how shall we eat? Harm to a single task of women’s textile work may seem a small matter; yet if no one under Heaven raises silkworms, how shall we clothe ourselves? Herein lie the far-reaching vision and the greatness of emperors and kings.

Thus their fame spreads throughout the Central Realm, and their beneficence reaches the eight remotest regions: their achievements are extensive and profound. They settle all under Heaven as securely as Mount Tai and establish the realm within the Four Seas as firmly as a great rock: their foundations are deep, firm, and unshakable. They establish their enterprise in their own time and bequeath their dynastic succession to posterity. If one generation willingly builds upon and completes its forebears’ work, that generation enjoys peace, wealth, honor, and glory without end. If a hundred generations neither err nor forget, how could the stipends, rank, renown, and longevity enjoyed through those hundred generations ever be exhausted? Even through a thousand or ten thousand generations, it would always be so. Could those who disregard farming and rely upon expedient schemes and manipulative arts accomplish such an enterprise? Could they establish such foundations? Could they bequeath such a dynastic succession? This is why the emperors and kings of antiquity took rites, music, punishments, and government as the means for ordering the world …

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
法而未嘗以為傳心之法以精一執中為
傳心之法而未嘗以為心法之要其為心
法之要者其惟知重農事也歟昔者有周
識見乎此自后稷以農事為務歷世相傳
其君子則重稼穡之事其室家則躬織紝
之勤相與咨嗟相與歎息服習乎艱難詠
歌其勞苦以周公之聖臣輔成王之賢主
告戒則以農桑之候為先七月之詩可徵
也獻替則以小人之依為重無逸之書可
===
驗也太王之妃姜女而王季之妃則太任
也文王之妃太姒而武王之后則邑姜也
皆助其君而焦勞於內咸勤於家而休美
於外所以傳世三十歷年八百不獨有周
為然堯得此要命官造曆敬授人時所以
土堦三尺茅茨不翦而黎民於變也舜得
此要憂民阻饑播時百穀所以罔遊于逸
罔淫于樂而四方風動也禹得此要身親
稼穡盡力溝洫所以不崇宮室菲薄飲食
punctuated:
法，而未嘗以為傳心之法；以精一執中為傳心之法，而未嘗以為心法之要。其為心法之要者，其惟知重農事也歟！昔者有周識見乎此，自后稷以農事為務，歷世相傳。其君子則重稼穡之事，其室家則躬織紝之勤，相與咨嗟，相與歎息，服習乎艱難，詠歌其勞苦。以周公之聖臣，輔成王之賢主，告戒則以農桑之候為先，《七月》之詩可徵也；獻替則以小人之依為重，《無逸》之書可驗也。太王之妃姜女，而王季之妃則太任也；文王之妃太姒，而武王之后則邑姜也。皆助其君而焦勞於內，咸勤於家而休美於外，所以傳世三十，歷年八百。
不獨有周為然，堯得此要，命官造曆，敬授人時，所以土堦三尺，茅茨不翦，而黎民於變也。舜得此要，憂民阻饑，播時百穀，所以罔遊于逸，罔淫于樂，而四方風動也。禹得此要，身親稼穡，盡力溝洫，所以不崇宮室，菲薄飲食
translation_en:
…methods for governing the world, yet never regarded them as methods for transmitting the mind. They took refinement and singleness of purpose, and holding fast to the Mean, as methods for transmitting the mind, yet never regarded these as the essential point of the teaching of the mind. Was not its essential point simply to understand the importance of agriculture? In former times, the Zhou understood this. Beginning with Hou Ji, they made agriculture their task and passed this commitment down through successive generations. Their noblemen valued sowing and reaping, while the women of their households personally undertook the toil of weaving. Together they sighed and lamented, accustomed themselves to hardship, and sang of their labors. When the Duke of Zhou, a sage minister, assisted King Cheng, a worthy ruler, his admonitions gave priority to the seasons for farming and sericulture, as the poem “The Seventh Month” attests. In offering good counsel and correcting faults, he placed foremost that on which the common people depended, as the document “Against Ease” confirms. King Tai’s consort was a woman of the Jiang clan; Wang Ji’s consort was Tai Ren. King Wen’s consort was Tai Si, and King Wu’s queen was Yi Jiang. All assisted their rulers, toiling anxiously within the palace; all worked diligently within the household and won praise beyond it. Thus the dynasty continued for thirty generations and endured for eight hundred years.
This was not true of the Zhou alone. Yao grasped this essential point, appointed officials to construct a calendar, and reverently made the seasons known to the people. Thus, although his earthen steps were only three feet high and his thatched eaves were left untrimmed, the common people were transformed. Shun grasped this essential point, was concerned that the people suffered hunger, and had the various grains sown. Thus he did not wander in idleness or indulge excessively in pleasure, and the four quarters responded as if stirred by the wind. Yu grasped this essential point, personally engaged in sowing and reaping, and devoted all his strength to irrigation channels and ditches. Thus he did not make his palaces lofty, and kept his food and drink meager…

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而聲教四訖也湯得此要六事自責禱雨
桑林所以不邇聲色不殖貨利而萬邦惟
懷也堯之子丹朱不可傳也堯則傳之於
舜舜之子商均不可傳也舜則傳之於禹
若成湯則又聞而得此要也歟使桀為禹
後知重農事以守其傳必不瓊宮瑶臺酒
池肉林以殫民財也而禹之九有未必歸
之於湯使紂為湯裔知重農事以保其傳
必不實鹿臺之財盈鉅橋之粟以斂民怨
===
也而湯之萬方未必歸之於周而周之衰
又在幽王之寵褒姒婦無公事休其蠶織
之所致也是則帝之所以帝王之所以王
皆以所識所見在於重農事而為所傳心
法之要也歟若漢若唐若宋諸君或躬耕
籍田或敦勸農事或已身衣至澣濯或後
宮衣不曳地或繪無逸之圖或咏憫農之
詩亦不可謂之不知重農事也但隆虛文
而無實事求其知重農事而遠接帝王所
punctuated: 而聲教四訖也。湯得此要，六事自責，禱雨桑林，所以不邇聲色，不殖貨利，而萬邦惟懷也。堯之子丹朱不可傳也，堯則傳之於舜；舜之子商均不可傳也，舜則傳之於禹。若成湯，則又聞而得此要也歟？使桀為禹後，知重農事以守其傳，必不瓊宮瑶臺、酒池肉林，以殫民財也，而禹之九有未必歸之於湯；使紂為湯裔，知重農事以保其傳，必不實鹿臺之財、盈鉅橋之粟，以斂民怨也，而湯之萬方未必歸之於周。而周之衰，又在幽王之寵褒姒，婦無公事，休其蠶織之所致也。是則帝之所以帝、王之所以王，皆以所識所見在於重農事，而為所傳心法之要也歟？若漢、若唐、若宋諸君，或躬耕籍田，或敦勸農事，或已身衣至澣濯，或後宮衣不曳地，或繪《無逸》之圖，或咏《憫農》之詩，亦不可謂之不知重農事也。但隆虛文而無實事，求其知重農事而遠接帝王所
translation_en:
…and his moral influence and instruction reached the four quarters. Tang grasped this essential principle: he reproached himself on six counts and prayed for rain at Sanglin. Thus he kept away from music and sensual pleasures, did not accumulate wealth for profit, and won the allegiance of the myriad states. Yao’s son Danzhu was unfit to receive the succession, so Yao passed it to Shun; Shun’s son Shangjun was unfit to receive the succession, so Shun passed it to Yu. As for Cheng Tang, did he too grasp this essential principle through what he had heard? Had Jie, as Yu’s descendant, understood the importance of agriculture and thereby preserved his inheritance, he surely would not have exhausted the people’s wealth on jade palaces and jeweled terraces, wine pools and forests of meat; Yu’s nine domains would then not necessarily have passed to Tang. Had Zhou, as Tang’s descendant, understood the importance of agriculture and thereby safeguarded his inheritance, he surely would not have filled the Deer Terrace with treasure and the Juqiao granaries with grain, thereby gathering the people’s resentment; Tang’s myriad regions would then not necessarily have passed to the Zhou dynasty. The decline of Zhou, moreover, resulted from King You’s favoring Bao Si: although women had no role in public affairs, she abandoned her silkworm raising and weaving. Was it not, then, their recognition and understanding of the importance of agriculture that made the ancient emperors true emperors and the kings true kings, and constituted the essential principle of the teaching of the mind that they transmitted?

As for the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song, some personally plowed the imperial ritual field; some earnestly encouraged agriculture; some wore their own garments until they required washing [?]; some had the women of the palace wear garments whose hems did not trail on the ground; some commissioned illustrations of Against Idleness; and some chanted the poem Pitying the Farmers. They too cannot be said to have failed to recognize the importance of agriculture. Yet they exalted empty forms without substantive action. If we seek those who understood the importance of agriculture and reached back across the ages to carry on what the ancient emperors and kings…

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
傳之緖者其惟我朝
列聖乎
太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸
孝慈高皇后助成帝業於農桑之艱難知之詳
悉所以躬行實踐也至告戒訓飭也詳
聖聖相承率由此法故
宗社奠安民物庶富殆同天長而地久也較之
前代帝王為有邁而漢唐宋風斯下矣愚
何幸身親見之
===
表
擬宋以曹彬為樞密院使謝表
祁仁
同考試官教諭趙批表佳
考試官學正陳批表得駢儷體
考試官教授黄批典雅可觀
伏以
握兵西府班聯三省之榮進秩北樞眷出
六卿之右非全才如旦奭詎可濫膺必碩
punctuated:
傳之緖者，其惟我朝列聖乎！太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸，孝慈高皇后助成帝業，於農桑之艱難知之詳悉，所以躬行實踐也至，告戒訓飭也詳。聖聖相承，率由此法，故宗社奠安，民物庶富，殆同天長而地久也。較之前代帝王為有邁，而漢唐宋風斯下矣。愚何幸身親見之！

表
擬宋以曹彬為樞密院使謝表
祁仁
同考試官教諭趙批：表佳。
考試官學正陳批：表得駢儷體。
考試官教授黄批：典雅可觀。

伏以：握兵西府，班聯三省之榮；進秩北樞，眷出六卿之右。非全才如旦奭，詎可濫膺？必碩
translation_en:
…those who carry forward the tradition they transmitted—surely these are the successive sage sovereigns of our dynasty! Taizu, the Gao Emperor, rose like a dragon in the Huai region, and Empress Xiaoci Gao helped establish the imperial enterprise. They knew thoroughly the hardships of farming and sericulture; hence their personal practice was most complete, and their admonitions and instructions most detailed. Sage sovereign succeeded sage sovereign, all following this example. title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
望似臯夔庶幾允稱顧茲
特授未遂堅辭竊念臣彬蠢爾武夫遭此
昌運提戈有志幼竊虛名學劍無成長慙
實用從
龍飛于洛上近依
駿德之光華息虎闘于江南深仗
廟謨之密勿囊韜弓矢幸奏捷於麒麟舟載
圖書敢伐功於汗馬行同潘美罪比全斌
甫及凱還遽蒙
===
優賜方愧報
恩之無地豈期申
命之自
天
渙汗下臨淵氷中惕茲盖伏遇
〇〇〇〇
聰明神武
仁厚謙恭撫治乘時乃太平之
天子誕生應祝真天縱之
punctuated: 望似臯夔，庶幾允稱。顧茲特授，未遂堅辭。竊念臣彬，蠢爾武夫，遭此昌運。提戈有志，幼竊虛名；學劍無成，長慙實用。從龍飛于洛上，近依駿德之光華；息虎闘于江南，深仗廟謨之密勿。囊韜弓矢，幸奏捷於麒麟；舟載圖書，敢伐功於汗馬？行同潘美，罪比全斌。甫及凱還，遽蒙優賜。方愧報恩之無地，豈期申命之自天？渙汗下臨，淵氷中惕。茲盖伏遇〇〇〇〇，聰明神武，仁厚謙恭，撫治乘時，乃太平之天子；誕生應祝，真天縱之
translation_en:
…with prestige like that of Gao Yao and Kui, one might nearly be worthy of the appointment. Yet this special appointment has come to me, and my firm request to decline it has not prevailed. I humbly reflect that I, your servant Bin, am but an uncouth military man who has encountered this flourishing age. Aspiring to take up the spear, in youth I undeservedly acquired an empty reputation; achieving nothing in swordsmanship, in maturity I am ashamed of my practical usefulness. Following Your Majesty’s dragon flight at Luoyang, I drew close to the radiance of your magnificent virtue; in stilling the clash of tigers in Jiangnan, I relied deeply upon the court’s painstaking strategic counsels. With bows and arrows returned to their cases, I was fortunate to announce victory at the Qilin Hall; with books and documents loaded aboard my boats, how could I boast of merit won by warhorses? My conduct was like Pan Mei’s; my culpability comparable to Wang Quanbin’s. No sooner had I returned in triumph than I received generous rewards. Just as I was ashamed to have no means of repaying your favor, how could I have expected a further command from Heaven? Your irrevocable decree descended, while inwardly I trembled as though approaching a deep abyss or treading thin ice.
This is because I have humbly encountered 〇〇〇〇 [honorific wording unrepresented?], intelligent and divinely martial, benevolent and generous, modest and respectful. Bringing order in accord with the times, you are indeed the Son of Heaven of an age of great peace; born in answer to prayers, you are truly one whom Heaven has endowed…

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖人洞然心地之虚明九門盡闢卓矣化功之
炳烺兩曜争明舉杯酒而釋兵拳保全宿
將用縉紳以持相軸隆重儒臣不為言語
文字之工真得誠正脩齊之學書藏金匱
孝友夙成布綠葦蕉儉勤懋著讀虞書而
嗟堯舜深嘉法網之疎幸國學而賛孔顔
肇啓人文之盛五星奎聚四海波恬還羲
黃以上之淳風洗秦漢以来之陋治求賢
若渴賤何棄乎布衣涖事惟能粗不遺於
===
介胄遂令重寄猥及庸才臣彬敢不俯瀝
蟻忱仰酬
鴻造旌麾制勝烏敢辭百戰之勞帷幄運籌
庶有裨萬全之計伏願
聖武布昭乎遐邇
王靈丕振乎華夷地厚天高莫象無前之偉
績民安國泰永綿不拔之丕圖臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
punctuated: 聖人。洞然心地之虚明，九門盡闢；卓矣化功之炳烺，兩曜争明。舉杯酒而釋兵拳，保全宿將；用縉紳以持相軸，隆重儒臣。不為言語文字之工，真得誠正脩齊之學。書藏金匱，孝友夙成；布綠葦蕉，儉勤懋著。讀虞書而嗟堯舜，深嘉法網之疎；幸國學而賛孔顔，肇啓人文之盛。五星奎聚，四海波恬。還羲黃以上之淳風，洗秦漢以来之陋治。求賢若渴，賤何棄乎布衣？涖事惟能，粗不遺於介胄。遂令重寄，猥及庸才。臣彬敢不俯瀝蟻忱，仰酬鴻造？旌麾制勝，烏敢辭百戰之勞？帷幄運籌，庶有裨萬全之計。伏願聖武布昭乎遐邇，王靈丕振乎華夷。地厚天高，莫象無前之偉績；民安國泰，永綿不拔之丕圖。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉
translation_en:
…sage. Your mind is open, unclouded, and luminous, its nine gates all thrown wide; splendid indeed is the brilliance of your transforming achievement, rivaling the sun and moon. Over a cup of wine you released veteran generals from military authority [?], preserving them unharmed; you entrusted the direction of government to scholar-officials, according high honor to Confucian ministers. You do not pursue mere skill in speech and writing, but have truly mastered the learning of making intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating oneself, and regulating the family. The document stored in the golden coffer attests to your early attainment of filial devotion and brotherly affection; plain cloth and reed or plantain furnishings [?] conspicuously display your frugality and diligence. Reading the Documents of Yu, you admired Yao and Shun and deeply commended the looseness of their legal net; visiting the Directorate of Education, you praised Confucius and Yan Hui, inaugurating a flourishing age of civilized learning. The five planets gather in the Kui constellation; throughout the Four Seas the waves are calm. You restore the unspoiled ways of the age of Fuxi and the Yellow Emperor and earlier, sweeping away the defective governance prevailing since Qin and Han. Thirsting for worthy men, how could you reject the commoner because of his humble standing? In appointing men to duties, you consider ability alone, passing over no armored warrior because of his roughness. Thus a weighty trust has undeservedly fallen upon a man of mediocre talent.

How could your servant Bin dare fail to pour forth his antlike sincerity below, repaying your vast beneficence above? Commanding beneath the banners to secure victory, how could I shrink from the toil of a hundred battles? Devising strategy within the command tent, I hope to contribute to plans ensuring complete success.

I humbly pray that your sagely martial prowess may shine far and near, and that your royal might may resound throughout the Chinese and non-Chinese realms. Neither the earth’s depth nor Heaven’s height can furnish a likeness for your unprecedented achievements. May the people enjoy peace and the realm tranquility, and may your unshakable imperial enterprise endure forever. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain his utmost fervor, awe, and trembling, and respectfully presents…

詩禮春秋之文及我

而書伏誅之類是也有謂内夏外夷者於
女貞沙州之來而書入貢之類是也至如
重韓通李筠之忠節而大書之所謂扶天

translation_en:
His Majesty personally wielded his imperial brush to provide the opening for this great work. I, in my ignorance, once bowed with clasped hands and touched my head to the ground, proclaiming: “How great are the imperial words! How unified in purpose are the imperial words! Are they not the means to establish the mind of Heaven and Earth, to establish the ultimate standard for the people, and to inaugurate peace for all ages? They follow the same principle as the writings of the ages of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties, resplendent in the Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites, and Spring and Autumn Annals, and as the proclamations of our sagely ancestors and divine forebears: all serve as great guiding principles and models, handed down to establish instruction for the world.”

I have reverently read the imperially composed preface. Its reference to punishing disorder and chastising rebellion is exemplified by recording that rebellious ministers and treacherous sons “suffered execution” when they were defeated. Its reference to treating the Chinese as insiders and the non-Chinese as outsiders is exemplified by recording the arrival of the Jurchens and the people of Shazhou as “coming to present tribute.” As for esteeming the loyalty and integrity of Han Tong and Li Yun and prominently recording them, this is what is meant by upholding heavenly principle and restraining human desires. Applying strict judgment to the deposition and enthronement involving the founding emperor of Song and the ruler of Zhou, and recording them explicitly—is this not what is meant by rectifying names and stations so as to establish the cardinal bonds and constant norms? Here lies an approximation of Master Zhu’s intent; here lies support for the Sage’s classic. In recording the events of four hundred and eight years, every inclusion and every deletion accords with this Way; the examples cannot be exhaustively enumerated. I have merely taken up the opening events in response to the matters raised by your illuminating question. As for the general …

text:

元之史及
皇明實録是也有曰得天下有救世之功者每
進之若宋太祖於開寶八年大書之是也
宋主中華金元分註於宋年之下所謂中
國為正統夷狄不得紀元也金虜據汴宋
國猶從正統之法所謂中國之統未絕猶
繫之中國也若至夷狄全有天下中國統
絕然後以統繫之非元并六合厓山已亡
===
之後乎中國有義兵起即夷之於列國非
兵起中華清肅夷風之時乎序例所載固
曰不同然序之所謂乃一書之大義例之
所載乃書法之微旨正如大學綱領統乎
條目而條目属於綱領孰謂義不可相通
而為用耶是以正道由之而明風俗以之
而阜誠億萬世垂教之大典然編秩浩瀚
如春秋大義數十炳若日星舉其大要不
過褒貶一言而已昔人讀春秋有曰一字
punctuated:
例所載，有曰：「事迹悉據舊史。」若宋遼金元之史及皇明實録是也。有曰：「得天下有救世之功者，每進之。」若宋太祖於開寶八年大書之是也。宋主中華，金元分註於宋年之下，所謂中國為正統，夷狄不得紀元也。金虜據汴，宋國猶從正統之法，所謂中國之統未絕，猶繫之中國也。若至夷狄全有天下，中國統絕，然後以統繫之，非元并六合、厓山已亡之後乎？中國有義兵起，即夷之於列國，非兵起中華、清肅夷風之時乎？
序例所載，固曰不同，然序之所謂，乃一書之大義；例之所載，乃書法之微旨。正如大學綱領統乎條目，而條目属於綱領，孰謂義不可相通而為用耶？是以正道由之而明，風俗以之而阜，誠億萬世垂教之大典。然編秩浩瀚，如春秋大義數十，炳若日星；舉其大要，不過褒貶一言而已。昔人讀春秋，有曰：「一字
translation_en:
…the editorial principles include the statement: “All accounts of events are based on the old histories.” These include the histories of the Song, Liao, Jin, and Yuan, as well as the Veritable Records of the August Ming. They also state: “Those who gained All under Heaven and rendered service in saving the age are regularly accorded higher standing.” An example is the prominent entry concerning Emperor Taizu of the Song under the eighth year of Kaibao. The Song ruled the Chinese heartland, while the Jin and Yuan are separately recorded in subordinate annotations beneath the Song years. This expresses the principle that China holds the legitimate succession and that the barbarians may not supply the chronological framework. When the Jin barbarians occupied Bian, the Song state was still treated according to the rules for the legitimate succession: so long as China’s succession had not been severed, it remained attached to China. Only when the barbarians possessed all the realm and China’s succession had ended was the succession attached to them. Was this not after the Yuan had united the realm and Yashan had already fallen? Once righteous armies arose in China, they were immediately reduced to the standing of one among the various states. Was this not when armies arose in the Chinese heartland to purge barbarian customs?
What the preface and the editorial principles contain admittedly differs. Yet what the preface sets forth is the central meaning of the entire book, while what the editorial principles contain is the subtle purport of its methods of historical writing. This is just like the Great Learning, in which the guiding principles encompass the particular articles, and the articles fall under the guiding principles. Who could say that their meanings cannot inform one another and function together? Through this, the correct Way is clarified and social customs flourish. It is truly a great canon that transmits instruction for countless generations. Yet although its volumes are vast, its several dozen major principles, like those of the Spring and Autumn Annals, shine as brightly as the sun and stars. To state their essential point, they amount simply to praise and blame. A reader of the Spring and Autumn Annals in former times once said: “A single character…”

相關也其計畫相聞也分雖異姓義若同
氣其所相尚不在於和乎嘗觀之古矣有
虞之朝九官濟濟百僚師師在位皆揖讓
之風其和也何如有周之廷士讓為大夫
大夫讓為卿三千人如一心之契其和也
何若三代既還世道日降士風不復古矣
若鄧艾平蜀鍾會害之王濬平吳王渾劾
===
之則所謂功侔而相猜者信有之矣其間
能寬嚴相濟而同心輔政者僅有如丙吉
魏相其人焉李宗閔入翰院李德裕銜之
王安石居政府呂惠卿訟之則所謂勢並
而相軋者誠有之矣其間能協心佐理而
讓直濟文者僅有如房玄齡杜如晦其人
焉廉頗藺相如皆趙賢臣相如有功位列
頗上頗不自揣欲面辱之何其私己也相
如乃引避不與之爭其知先國家之計乎
punctuated: 患其和德之不協也哉？請因明問而紬繹之。夫同官為寮寀，其班列相近也，其職務相關也，其計畫相聞也。分雖異姓，義若同氣，其所相尚不在於和乎？嘗觀之古矣：有虞之朝，九官濟濟，百僚師師，在位皆揖讓之風，其和也何如？有周之廷，士讓為大夫，大夫讓為卿，三千人如一心之契，其和也何若？三代既還，世道日降，士風不復古矣。若鄧艾平蜀，鍾會害之；王濬平吳，王渾劾之，則所謂功侔而相猜者，信有之矣。其間能寬嚴相濟而同心輔政者，僅有如丙吉、魏相其人焉。李宗閔入翰院，李德裕銜之；王安石居政府，呂惠卿訟之，則所謂勢並而相軋者，誠有之矣。其間能協心佐理而讓直濟文者，僅有如房玄齡、杜如晦其人焉。廉頗、藺相如皆趙賢臣，相如有功，位列頗上，頗不自揣，欲面辱之，何其私己也！相如乃引避，不與之爭，其知先國家之計乎？
translation_en: …why worry that they will fail to accord in harmonious virtue? Allow me to draw out this matter in response to your enlightened question. Those who hold office together are colleagues: their ranks are close, their duties interconnected, and their plans known to one another. Though they belong to different families, their moral bonds resemble those of brothers. Is harmony not what they should esteem in one another? I have considered the examples of antiquity. At the court of Youyu, the nine officers were dignified and the hundred officials mutually respectful; all who held office displayed a spirit of courtesy and deference. How great was their harmony! At the court of Zhou, servicemen yielded to one another in advancement to grand master, and grand masters in advancement to minister; three thousand men were united as though of one mind. How great was their harmony! Since the Three Dynasties, the moral condition of the world has declined daily, and the conduct of scholars has ceased to resemble that of antiquity. When Deng Ai pacified Shu, Zhong Hui brought about his destruction; when Wang Jun pacified Wu, Wang Hun impeached him. Thus there truly have been men who, equal in achievement, suspected one another. Among them, only such men as Bing Ji and Wei Xiang could temper severity with leniency and assist in government with a common purpose. When Li Zongmin entered the Hanlin Academy, Li Deyu resented him; when Wang Anshi held office in the chief council, Lü Huiqing brought accusations against him. Thus there truly have been men who, equal in power, undermined one another. Among them, only such men as Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui could assist in government with united hearts, using deference and uprightness to complement cultivated ability [?]. Lian Po and Lin Xiangru were both worthy ministers of Zhao. Because of his achievements, Xiangru was ranked above Lian Po. Lian Po, failing to take his own measure, wanted to insult him to his face. How selfish he was! Xiangru instead withdrew and avoided him, refusing to contend with him. Did he not understand that the interests of the state must come first?

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
冦恂賈復皆漢元勲復部將有罪為恂所
戮復不自反欲手刃之何其計踈也恂乃
稱疾不與之見其知急公家之義乎佐唐
中興如郭子儀李光弼者雖曰齊著將業
而其私隙終不釋然若杜富諸公平居相
稱而議事公言無私則真得和而不同之
意矣其所處盖尤善焉佐宋恢復如劉光
世韓世忠者雖曰同擅將略而其宿釁終
有圭角若韓范諸賢上殿争事而下殿和
===
氣如初則真得公爾忘私之義矣其所事
盖尤美焉他如范景仁之於司馬光異姓
相契不啻兄弟然論鍾律之争則反復相
非非為私也道不苟同也張浚之於趙鼎
同朝相善有如手足及因吕祉之𮠑則彼
此相左非為已也議不苟合也是則數君
子之相與得失較然要之暫異而随同始
殊而終合皆不至甚咈於和也惟以虞周
之臣而比擬之則不無少貶焉肆我
punctuated: 冦恂、賈復皆漢元勲，復部將有罪，為恂所戮，復不自反，欲手刃之，何其計踈也！恂乃稱疾，不與之見，其知急公家之義乎？佐唐中興如郭子儀、李光弼者，雖曰齊著將業，而其私隙終不釋然。若杜、富諸公，平居相稱，而議事公言無私，則真得和而不同之意矣，其所處盖尤善焉。佐宋恢復如劉光世、韓世忠者，雖曰同擅將略，而其宿釁終有圭角。若韓、范諸賢，上殿争事，而下殿和氣如初，則真得公爾忘私之義矣，其所事盖尤美焉。他如范景仁之於司馬光，異姓相契，不啻兄弟，然論鍾律之争，則反復相非，非為私也，道不苟同也。張浚之於趙鼎，同朝相善，有如手足，及因吕祉之𮠑，則彼此相左，非為已也，議不苟合也。是則數君子之相與，得失較然。要之，暫異而随同，始殊而終合，皆不至甚咈於和也。惟以虞、周之臣而比擬之，則不無少貶焉。肆我
translation_en: Kou Xun and Jia Fu were both founding heroes of the Han. A subordinate commander of Jia Fu committed an offense and was executed by Kou Xun. Rather than examining his own conduct, Jia Fu wished to kill Kou Xun with his own hands. How ill-considered his intentions were! Kou Xun thereupon pleaded illness and declined to meet him. Did he not understand the duty of putting the state's affairs first? Those who assisted the Tang restoration, such as Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi, both achieved distinction as generals, yet their personal estrangement was never entirely resolved. Lords Du and Fu, however, praised one another in ordinary dealings, while speaking impartially and without private bias when deliberating on affairs. They truly grasped the meaning of harmony without conformity; their way of conducting themselves was especially commendable. Those who assisted the Song recovery, such as Liu Guangshi and Han Shizhong, both excelled in military strategy, yet their old antagonisms continued to produce friction. Worthies such as Han and Fan, however, disputed affairs when they entered the throne hall, but left it as amicably disposed as before. They truly grasped the duty of forgetting private interests in devotion to the public good; their conduct was especially admirable. Another example is Fan Jingren's relationship with Sima Guang: though of different surnames, their affinity was no less than that of brothers. Yet in their dispute over bells and pitch standards, they repeatedly criticized one another. This was not for private ends: they would not assent heedlessly on matters of principle. Zhang Jun and Zhao Ding, serving at the same court, were on affectionate terms, like brothers. Yet over the affair involving Lü Zhi [?], they took opposing positions. This was not for personal advantage: they would not agree heedlessly in their deliberations. Thus the merits and failings in these gentlemen's dealings with one another are clearly apparent. In general, they differed temporarily but soon agreed, diverged at first but ultimately came together; none went so far as gravely to violate harmony. title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
國家
列聖相承群賢畢用揖遜興於朝仁讓洽於外
其寮寀之協和固遠出漢唐宋之上矣然
而明問之意猶欲舉今日之臣而儕諸虞
周之列此在當路執政之所優為豈愚生
所敢知哉雖然竊聞之孔子曰公則說孟
子曰至誠而不動者未之有也夫知誠之
可以動人則臨政遇事過必歸我善必歸
彼而所以積吾誠者惟恐不至也知公之
===
可以悅人則群居旅處私隙勿萌小嫌勿
計而所以仗吾公者惟恐不盡也若然則
意見雖異不害其為同行事雖殊不失其
為合僚寀之情分於是乎可得國家之大
計於是乎不妨尚何患德讓之不虞周同
心之不同臣也哉管見如此執事以為何
如
第三問
鄭文標
punctuated:
國家列聖相承，群賢畢用，揖遜興於朝，仁讓洽於外，其寮寀之協和固遠出漢唐宋之上矣。然而明問之意，猶欲舉今日之臣而儕諸虞周之列，此在當路執政之所優為，豈愚生所敢知哉？雖然，竊聞之，孔子曰：「公則說。」孟子曰：「至誠而不動者，未之有也。」夫知誠之可以動人，則臨政遇事，過必歸我，善必歸彼，而所以積吾誠者惟恐不至也。知公之可以悅人，則群居旅處，私隙勿萌，小嫌勿計，而所以仗吾公者惟恐不盡也。若然，則意見雖異，不害其為同；行事雖殊，不失其為合。僚寀之情分於是乎可得，國家之大計於是乎不妨。尚何患德讓之不虞周，同心之不同臣也哉？管見如此，執事以為何如？
第三問
鄭文標
translation_en:
…in our dynasty, successive sage sovereigns have followed one another, and all worthy men have been employed. Courteous deference flourishes at court, while benevolence and yielding prevail beyond it. The harmony among its officials assuredly far surpasses that of the Han, Tang, and Song. Yet the intent of your enlightened question is still to raise the ministers of today to the ranks of those of Yu and Zhou. This is something those in authority who direct government can readily accomplish; how could an ignorant student such as I presume to understand it?
Nevertheless, I have heard Confucius say, “If you are impartial, people will be pleased,” and Mengzi say, “Never has there been one who was utterly sincere yet failed to move others.” Knowing that sincerity can move people, when administering government and handling affairs one must always take faults upon oneself and give credit to others, fearing only that one has not gone far enough in cultivating sincerity. Knowing that impartiality can please people, when living and associating with others one must allow no private grievances to arise and take no account of petty resentments, fearing only that one has not fully upheld impartiality. If this is done, differences of opinion will not impair unity, and differences in conduct will not destroy concord. Fellow officials can thereby achieve mutual affection, and the great plans of the state will suffer no obstruction. Why then worry that virtue and deference will fall short of those of Yu and Zhou, or that unity of purpose will fall short of that of their ministers [?]? Such is my limited view. What do you, sir, think of it?
Third Policy Question
Zheng Wenbiao

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭崔批敷演畧無凝滯真博洽之士歟
考試官學正陳批考據詳悉足見學識
考試官教授黃批論功業必本學術之正異日當有可觀
觀學優則仕之言則知用世者必由於學
觀不學無術之則知濟世者尤賴於學
夫學以明道而仕以行其學也學術之淺
深功業大小攸係也學術固可見於功業
矣豈有功業而不本於學術者哉幼而學
===
之壯而行之脩之身行之家推之於國於
天下其道一而已矣請因明問而歷陳之
賢人君子出而康濟斯民兼善天下未始
不由於學問中來也本於學問則其寅亮
也有具其調燮也有本其經綸也有要為
上則為德為下則為民何施而不可哉故
禹臯之謨禹臯之學術也而雍熈之治泰
和之休實基於都俞吁咈之言賡歌戒敕
之語也伊周之訓伊周之學術也而兆民
punctuated:
同考試官教諭崔批：敷演畧無凝滯，真博洽之士歟！
考試官學正陳批：考據詳悉，足見學識。
考試官教授黃批：論功業必本學術之正，異日當有可觀。

觀學優則仕之言，則知用世者必由於學；觀不學無術之，則知濟世者尤賴於學。夫學以明道，而仕以行其學也。學術之淺深，功業大小攸係也。學術固可見於功業矣，豈有功業而不本於學術者哉？幼而學之，壯而行之，脩之身，行之家，推之於國於天下，其道一而已矣。請因明問而歷陳之。

賢人君子出而康濟斯民，兼善天下，未始不由於學問中來也。本於學問，則其寅亮也有具，其調燮也有本，其經綸也有要。為上則為德，為下則為民，何施而不可哉？故禹臯之謨，禹臯之學術也，而雍熈之治、泰和之休，實基於都俞吁咈之言、賡歌戒敕之語也。伊周之訓，伊周之學術也，而兆民
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor: His exposition proceeds without the slightest impediment. Truly a man of broad and thorough learning!
Comment by Examiner Chen, School Instructor: His examination of the evidence is detailed and thorough, amply demonstrating his learning and understanding.
Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: In discussing achievements, he invariably grounds them in the rectitude of learning. In days to come, he should have accomplishments worth observing.

Considering the saying, “When learning is ample, take office,” we know that service to the world must proceed from learning. Considering “Without learning, there is no skill” [?], we know that bringing aid to the world depends still more upon learning. Learning serves to illuminate the Way, while office serves to put one's learning into practice. The magnitude of one's achievements depends upon the depth of one's learning. Learning can indeed be discerned in achievements; how could there be achievements that are not grounded in learning? What one studies in youth, one puts into practice in maturity: cultivating it in oneself, practicing it within one's family, and extending it to the state and to all under Heaven. The Way is one throughout. Allow me to respond to your enlightened question by setting this out in detail.

When worthy men and gentlemen come forward to bring peace and aid to these people and extend goodness throughout the world, their actions invariably spring from learning. Grounded in learning, they possess the means to assist their sovereign with reverence, a foundation for harmonizing affairs, and guiding principles for ordering the realm. In serving those above, they work for virtue; in serving those below, they work for the people. In what undertaking could they fail? Thus the counsels of Yu and Gao Yao embody their learning. The harmonious and splendid government and the blessings of supreme peace were founded upon their words of praise, assent, caution, and dissent, and upon their exchanges of songs and words of admonition. title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之懷萬姓之服實兆於允德協下之陳立
政任人之訓也九合諸侯一匡天下此管
仲之伯業矣而管子一書非其學之所蘊
乎齊國大治以其君顯此晏子之相業矣
而晏子一書非其學之所藉乎然禹皐伊
周之學正故其事功俊偉之可觀管仲晏
子之學駁故其規模狹隘之可鄙其可同
年而語哉嬴秦無道灰燼六經周勃木強
其知學為何事雖左袒一呼漢鼎不搖而
===
自防之蠢安能免疎昧之譏漢武嗣位尊
崇方士霍光無術其視學為何物雖漢昭
之托始終不移而寵利自居安能免猜疑
之患然勃也專尚詐力小節奚觀光也憑
仗忠義大節可取其可同時而語哉誓志
渡江擊楫中流興復之舉非細故也祖逖
其知春秋復讎之義矣而謂清談者能之
乎提兵八千摧敵百萬淮淝之捷非細事
也謝玄其達大易見幾之旨矣而謂談玄
punctuated: 之懷、萬姓之服，實兆於允德協下之陳、立政任人之訓也。九合諸侯，一匡天下，此管仲之伯業矣，而《管子》一書，非其學之所蘊乎？齊國大治，以其君顯，此晏子之相業矣，而《晏子》一書，非其學之所藉乎？然禹皐伊周之學正，故其事功俊偉之可觀；管仲晏子之學駁，故其規模狹隘之可鄙。其可同年而語哉？嬴秦無道，灰燼六經；周勃木強，其知學為何事？雖左袒一呼，漢鼎不搖，而自防之蠢，安能免疎昧之譏？漢武嗣位，尊崇方士；霍光無術，其視學為何物？雖漢昭之托，始終不移，而寵利自居，安能免猜疑之患？然勃也專尚詐力，小節奚觀；光也憑仗忠義，大節可取。其可同時而語哉？誓志渡江，擊楫中流，興復之舉，非細故也。祖逖其知《春秋》復讎之義矣，而謂清談者能之乎？提兵八千，摧敵百萬，淮淝之捷，非細事也。謝玄其達《大易》見幾之旨矣，而謂談玄
translation_en:
…the people’s attachment and the submission of all the myriad surnames were indeed foreshadowed in their statements on sincere virtue and harmony with those below, and their instructions on establishing government and appointing men. Nine times assembling the feudal lords and once setting the realm aright: these were Guan Zhong’s achievements as a hegemon’s minister. Does not the book Guanzi contain the substance of his learning? Bringing excellent order to the state of Qi and thereby bringing distinction to its ruler: these were Yan Zi’s achievements as chief minister. Was not the book Yanzi the repository of the learning on which he drew? Yet the learning of Yu, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou was orthodox, and thus their accomplishments were outstanding and worthy of admiration. The learning of Guan Zhong and Yan Zi was mixed, and thus the scope of their undertakings was narrow and deserving of disdain. Can they possibly be spoken of on equal terms?

The Qin of the Ying house lacked the Way and reduced the Six Classics to ashes. Zhou Bo was blunt and obstinate: what did he know of the business of learning? Although, at his single call to bare the left arm, the Han dynasty stood unshaken, how could his foolishness in protecting himself escape the charge of ignorance? Emperor Wu of Han succeeded to the throne and exalted masters of esoteric arts. Huo Guang lacked learning: what regard did he have for it? Although he remained steadfast from beginning to end in carrying out the trust concerning Emperor Zhao of Han, he ensconced himself in imperial favor and advantage. How could he escape the troubles arising from suspicion? Yet Zhou Bo prized only deceit and force: what was there to admire in his lesser acts of integrity? Huo Guang relied upon loyalty and righteousness: his integrity in great matters deserves approval. Can they possibly be spoken of on equal terms?

Leading eight thousand troops and crushing an enemy a million strong, he won the victory at the Huai and Fei rivers—no minor affair. title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者能之乎孔明出師二表合伊訓說命之
旨足以扶炎劉再造之統趙普論語一部
窺聖賢脩治之道足以輔大宋維新之命
然孔明學術純正用於世而有餘趙普天
資暗合亦近似而可觀也至於李膺范滂
之徒恃剛介之資抱澄清之志平時自許
崢嶸磊落而黨錮之禍輡軻萬狀豈其學
之不逮哉時使然也晦菴元定之派紹聖
賢之傳明大學之道學問淵微義理精粹
===
而偽學之讐釁搆百端豈其學之不至哉
時使然也夫東都之事吹枯噓燼自相題
榜處世之道殆有所未盡者而紫陽之學
立身行道致君澤民豈人所能及哉故當
時之追恨不能無而千古之事業不能泯
也是則明體適用奚可視為虛談學術功
業烏可岐為二道故學術有淺深而事功
有大小時勢有順逆功業有難易也歟由
是而觀君子但當盡在己之所當為不可
punctuated:
者能之乎？孔明出師二表，合伊訓、說命之旨，足以扶炎劉再造之統；趙普論語一部，窺聖賢脩治之道，足以輔大宋維新之命。然孔明學術純正，用於世而有餘；趙普天資暗合，亦近似而可觀也。至於李膺、范滂之徒，恃剛介之資，抱澄清之志，平時自許崢嶸磊落，而黨錮之禍，輡軻萬狀，豈其學之不逮哉？時使然也。晦菴、元定之派，紹聖賢之傳，明大學之道，學問淵微，義理精粹，而偽學之讐，釁搆百端，豈其學之不至哉？時使然也。
夫東都之事，吹枯噓燼，自相題榜，處世之道殆有所未盡者；而紫陽之學，立身行道，致君澤民，豈人所能及哉？故當時之追恨不能無，而千古之事業不能泯也。是則明體適用，奚可視為虛談？學術功業，烏可岐為二道？故學術有淺深，而事功有大小；時勢有順逆，功業有難易也歟！由是而觀，君子但當盡在己之所當為，不可
translation_en:
…could those who discourse on mysteries have accomplished this? Kongming’s two Memorials on Dispatching the Army accorded with the purport of the Instructions of Yi and the Charge to Yue, and were sufficient to sustain the restored dynastic succession of the Liu house of Han, whose virtue was fire. Zhao Pu, with a single copy of the Analects, discerned the sages’ and worthies’ way of self-cultivation and government, sufficiently to assist the great Song’s renewed mandate. Yet Kongming’s learning was pure and correct, more than sufficient for practical application in the world; Zhao Pu’s natural endowments accorded with the Way without his fully understanding it, and this approximation, too, was worthy of regard. As for men such as Li Ying and Fan Pang, they relied on their firm and upright character and cherished the ambition to cleanse the realm. In ordinary times they prided themselves on their outstanding stature and open integrity, yet the disaster of the partisan proscriptions subjected them to countless hardships. Was this because their learning fell short? The times made it so. The school of Hui’an and Yuanding—Zhu Xi and Cai Yuanding—continued the transmission of the sages and worthies and elucidated the Way of the Great Learning. Their scholarship was profound and subtle, their understanding of moral principles refined and pure; yet enemies who branded their teaching “false learning” contrived disputes in a hundred ways. Was this because their learning had failed to reach perfection? The times made it so.
In the affairs of the Eastern Han, however, they blew upon withered wood and fanned dying embers, bestowing honorific appraisals upon one another; their way of conducting themselves in the world was perhaps not entirely adequate. But as for the learning of Ziyang—Zhu Xi—who could match him in establishing his character, practicing the Way, bringing his ruler to excellence, and benefiting the people? Thus, although those times could not be free of causes for retrospective regret, achievements enduring through the ages cannot be effaced. How, then, can clarifying fundamental principles and applying them in practice be regarded as empty talk? How can learning and achievement be divided into two separate paths? Learning may be shallow or profound, and accomplishments small or great; circumstances may be favorable or adverse, and achievements difficult or easy. Viewed in this light, the gentleman should simply fulfill all that lies within his own responsibility, and must not…

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
計事功之所難必盖蘊藉於胸中有素而
推行於事功有驗若廪之粟園之蔬随取
而随有也得於已者有其實則見於用者
有其功如庖之刀扁之劑屢試而屢效也
愚也生西土沐
皇風菁莪
聖化講明聖賢大學之至理服膺師友平昔之
格言固竊慕聖賢之事業矣萬宇春盎麗
日熈熈獨不能效春蟄秋蚓之一鳴乎但
===
思處囊之已久恨脫穎之無由惟執事先
生進教之幸甚
第四問
蔡欽
同考試官訓導黄批有考據有断制舉子對策如是他日行事可見矣
同考試官教諭趙批於先儒論諫事断制明白而意寓抑揚其素負可窺矣異時有言責幸毋忘于斯言
考試官學正陳批正義策随問随答是宜録出
考試官教授黄批忠諫之論期不負於初心
punctuated:
計事功之所難必。盖蘊藉於胸中有素，而推行於事功有驗，若廪之粟、園之蔬，随取而随有也。得於已者有其實，則見於用者有其功，如庖之刀、扁之劑，屢試而屢效也。愚也生西土，沐皇風，菁莪聖化，講明聖賢大學之至理，服膺師友平昔之格言，固竊慕聖賢之事業矣。萬宇春盎，麗日熈熈，獨不能效春蟄秋蚓之一鳴乎？但思處囊之已久，恨脫穎之無由，惟執事先生進教之，幸甚。
第四問
蔡欽
同考試官訓導黄批：「有考據，有断制，舉子對策如是，他日行事可見矣。」
同考試官教諭趙批：「於先儒論諫事，断制明白，而意寓抑揚，其素負可窺矣。異時有言責，幸毋忘于斯言。」
考試官學正陳批：「正義策，随問随答，是宜録出。」
考試官教授黄批：「忠諫之論，期不負於初心。」
translation_en:
…reckon upon achievements whose attainment cannot be assured. What has long been stored within the breast proves effective when put into practice, like grain in a granary or vegetables in a garden, available whenever one reaches for them. When what one has acquired within oneself has substance, its application produces results, like the cook’s knife or Bian Que’s prescriptions, effective each time they are tried.
I, in my ignorance, was born in the western lands and have bathed in the imperial influence and the sage’s transforming nurture of scholars, celebrated in the ode “Luxuriant Southernwood.” I have studied and clarified the ultimate principles of the sages’ and worthies’ Great Learning and taken to heart the enduring maxims of teachers and friends. Indeed, I have privately aspired to the undertakings of the sages and worthies. Spring fills the whole realm, and the bright sun shines warmly: can I alone not emulate the single cry of a creature stirring from spring hibernation or an earthworm in autumn? Yet I reflect that I have long remained within the bag and lament that I have had no means for my point to emerge. If you, honored gentlemen in charge, would grant me further instruction, I would be most fortunate.
Fourth Question
Cai Qin
Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “There is substantiation, and there is decisive judgment. When an examination candidate answers policy questions in this manner, one can foresee how he will conduct affairs in the future.”
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “In discussing earlier Confucian scholars’ remonstrances, his judgments are clear, while his meaning conveys both criticism and praise. One can glimpse the abilities and aspirations he has long possessed. If in the future he bears responsibility for remonstrance, may he not forget these words.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “A policy essay upholding correct principles, answering each question as it comes. This merits selection for inclusion in the record.”
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: “In this discussion of loyal remonstrance, I hope he will remain true to his original intention.”

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有愛君憂國之心而後敢言天下之事有
救時切務之言而後能愜天下之論何則
天下之事當國之政固人臣之所當言也
惟夫忠肝義膽以天下為己責以國計為
己憂然後其言感激痛切時務雖或犯宸
怒觸逆鱗不見合于時而天下士大夫之
清論自不能不翕然而歸之矣不然則首
鼠自然伏馬不言或雖言之而無益於事
不切於時欲免天下之譏誚且難尚何清
===
論之有哉執事發策及此甚盛心也請陳
之夫忠臣義士直言敢諫何代無之如賈
誼治安之疏董仲舒天人之策韓愈佛骨
之表劉蕡賢良之對垂今千百載矣其忠
愛之心經濟之略讀之凛然猶有生氣自
餘諫者若朱雲請斬張禹而折檻其論之
激非過也忠憤所發也彼陳禾論童貫而
至引裾或者失之過焉褚遂良爭立武后
而流血其言之苦非矯也忠誠所觸也彼
punctuated:
有愛君憂國之心，而後敢言天下之事；有救時切務之言，而後能愜天下之論。何則？天下之事，當國之政，固人臣之所當言也。惟夫忠肝義膽，以天下為己責，以國計為己憂，然後其言感激痛切時務，雖或犯宸怒、觸逆鱗，不見合于時，而天下士大夫之清論，自不能不翕然而歸之矣。不然，則首鼠自然伏馬不言，或雖言之而無益於事、不切於時，欲免天下之譏誚且難，尚何清論之有哉？執事發策及此，甚盛心也，請陳之。
夫忠臣義士，直言敢諫，何代無之？如賈誼治安之疏、董仲舒天人之策、韓愈佛骨之表、劉蕡賢良之對，垂今千百載矣。其忠愛之心、經濟之略，讀之凛然，猶有生氣。自餘諫者，若朱雲請斬張禹而折檻，其論之激，非過也，忠憤所發也。彼陳禾論童貫而至引裾，或者失之過焉。褚遂良爭立武后而流血，其言之苦，非矯也，忠誠所觸也。彼
translation_en:
Only with a heart that loves the ruler and cares for the state does one dare speak about the affairs of the realm; only with words that remedy the troubles of the age and address urgent business can one satisfy the judgment of the realm. Why is this? The affairs of the realm and the policies of those governing the state are certainly matters on which a subject ought to speak. Only when a man possesses loyal resolve and righteous courage, takes responsibility for the realm upon himself, and makes the state’s concerns his own will his words be impassioned and address current affairs with painful urgency. Though he may provoke imperial anger and touch the dragon’s reverse scales, finding no acceptance in his day, the impartial judgment of the realm’s scholar-officials cannot but converge in his favor. Otherwise, he will waver and remain silent [?]; or, even if he speaks, his words will benefit no undertaking and meet no present need. He will scarcely escape the realm’s ridicule—how could he win its favorable judgment? That you, honored examiners, have raised this matter in your policy question shows the depth of your concern. Allow me to set forth my views.
What age has lacked loyal ministers and righteous men who spoke frankly and dared to remonstrate? Such writings as Jia Yi’s Memorial on Good Government and Security, Dong Zhongshu’s Policy Responses on Heaven and Man, Han Yu’s Memorial on the Buddha’s Bone, and Liu Fen’s response in the examination for Worthy and Good men have come down to us over hundreds and thousands of years. Reading them, one feels awe at their loyal devotion and their plans for ordering the world; they still seem alive with vital force. Among other remonstrators, Zhu Yun requested the execution of Zhang Yu and broke a balustrade. The vehemence of his argument was no excess: it arose from loyal indignation. Chen He, however, denounced Tong Guan and went so far as to tug at the emperor’s robe; perhaps he erred through excess. Chu Suiliang opposed the enthronement of Empress Wu and shed blood. The anguish of his words was no affectation: it was prompted by sincere loyalty. That other man…

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
劉栖楚言晏朝而願碎首不免出於矯偽
唐太宗欲脩洛陽宮幾勞民矣張玄素以
隋事為喻而乎止之回天之力宜乎來魏
徵之歎宋真宗信受天書幾褻天矣孫奭
以天何言哉而陳曉之破人主之惑宜乎
致呂中之許永淳之際言路久壅李善感
因封五嶽而痛諫之時人得於創見安得
無鳳鳴朝陽之稱乎貞元之時陸贄奏忤
陽城因帥諫垣而力救之朝士幸其忠直
===
安得無天下太平之賀乎皇祐之初文彥
博取媚宮闈相體玷矣唐介獨力爭之雖
遭謫宦而真御史之稱天下翕然名節何
高也異時范仲淹余靖尹洙歐陽脩坐攻
執政相繼左遷蔡襄以四賢咏之士林傳
誦名節章章較之真御史奚忝哉熈寧之
朝李定驟除臺憲銓考紊矣蘇頌宋敏求
李大臨協力奏之雖遭落職而三舍人之
稱于時籍甚忠鯁何著也異時徐經孫陳
punctuated: 劉栖楚言晏朝而願碎首，不免出於矯偽。唐太宗欲脩洛陽宮，幾勞民矣。張玄素以隋事為喻而乎止之，回天之力，宜乎來魏徵之歎。宋真宗信受天書，幾褻天矣。孫奭以「天何言哉」而陳曉之，破人主之惑，宜乎致呂中之許。永淳之際，言路久壅，李善感因封五嶽而痛諫之，時人得於創見，安得無鳳鳴朝陽之稱乎？貞元之時，陸贄奏忤，陽城因帥諫垣而力救之，朝士幸其忠直，安得無天下太平之賀乎？皇祐之初，文彥博取媚宮闈，相體玷矣。唐介獨力爭之，雖遭謫宦，而真御史之稱天下翕然，名節何高也！異時，范仲淹、余靖、尹洙、歐陽脩坐攻執政，相繼左遷。蔡襄以四賢咏之，士林傳誦，名節章章，較之真御史奚忝哉？熈寧之朝，李定驟除臺憲，銓考紊矣。蘇頌、宋敏求、李大臨協力奏之，雖遭落職，而三舍人之稱于時籍甚，忠鯁何著也！異時，徐經孫、陳
translation_en: …Liu Qichu remonstrated against the late holding of court and offered to dash his head to pieces; this could hardly escape the charge of affectation and insincerity. Emperor Taizong of Tang wished to renovate the palace at Luoyang, nearly imposing onerous labor on the people. Zhang Xuansu invoked the example of the Sui dynasty and stopped him [?]. His power to turn back Heaven—that is, to change the sovereign’s mind—was indeed worthy of Wei Zheng’s admiration. Emperor Zhenzong of Song credulously accepted the heavenly writings, nearly profaning Heaven. Sun Shi explained matters to him with the words, “What does Heaven ever say?” His dispelling of the ruler’s delusion was indeed worthy of Lü Zhong’s praise. During the Yongchun era, the channels of remonstrance had long been blocked. Li Shangan vehemently remonstrated on the occasion of the conferral of titles upon the Five Sacred Peaks. People of the time witnessed something unprecedented: how could they fail to acclaim him as a phoenix singing toward the morning sun? During the Zhenyuan era, Lu Zhi’s memorial offended the sovereign. Yang Cheng thereupon led the remonstrance officials in vigorously defending him. The court officials rejoiced in his loyalty and uprightness: how could they fail to offer congratulations that all under Heaven was at peace? Early in the Huangyou era, Wen Yanbo sought favor within the palace women’s quarters, sullying the dignity of the chief councilor’s office. Tang Jie alone vigorously challenged him. Although he suffered demotion and banishment to a provincial post, all under Heaven unanimously acclaimed him as a “true censor.” How lofty were his reputation and integrity! At another time, Fan Zhongyan, Yu Jing, Yin Zhu, and Ouyang Xiu were successively demoted for attacking those who held power. Cai Xiang celebrated them in verse as the Four Worthies, and scholars passed the poem around and recited it. Their reputation and integrity shone clearly; how were they inferior to the “true censor”? During the Xining reign, Li Ding was abruptly appointed to the Censorate, throwing the procedures for selection and assessment into disorder. Su Song, Song Minqiu, and Li Dalin joined forces in submitting memorials against this. Although they were dismissed from office, their fame as the “Three Secretariat Drafters” was widespread at the time. How conspicuous were their loyalty and forthrightness! title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
著陳茂濂坐議公田相繼引去時人以三
烈號之萬口一談忠鯁諤諤方之三舍人
奚愧哉他如在慶元間伏闕上書白趙汝
愚之冤者楊宏中周端朝張衟林仲麟蔣
傅徐範其人也時雖黜五百里而六君子
之名洋溢中外豈其要譽於人哉言盖補
乎當世之務也在寳祐間伏閤陳事劾丁
大全之奸者陳宜中黃鏞林則祖曾唯劉
黻陳宗其人也時雖編管遠州而六君子
===
之稱傳播遐邇豈其釣名於眾哉言盖切
乎當□之政也夫有忠義之心斯有鯁直
之言若數公之論諫事雖不同而皆發於
忠義見雖不一而皆歸於鯁直丹心烈日
勁氣秋霜嚮使得君而行之其匡救裨補
宜亦多矣奈何道與時違動遭齟齬名雖
愜於清論事無益於人國可慨也哉雖然
數公之論諫固忠矣直矣而於所以論諫
之道亦容有不盡也孔子曰勿欺也而犯
punctuated:
著、陳茂濂坐議公田，相繼引去。時人以三烈號之，萬口一談，忠鯁諤諤，方之三舍人奚愧哉？他如在慶元間伏闕上書，白趙汝愚之冤者，楊宏中、周端朝、張衟、林仲麟、蔣傅、徐範其人也。時雖黜五百里，而六君子之名洋溢中外，豈其要譽於人哉？言盖補乎當世之務也。在寳祐間伏閤陳事，劾丁大全之奸者，陳宜中、黃鏞、林則祖、曾唯、劉黻、陳宗其人也。時雖編管遠州，而六君子之稱傳播遐邇，豈其釣名於眾哉？言盖切乎當□之政也。

夫有忠義之心，斯有鯁直之言。若數公之論諫，事雖不同，而皆發於忠義；見雖不一，而皆歸於鯁直。丹心烈日，勁氣秋霜。嚮使得君而行之，其匡救裨補宜亦多矣。奈何道與時違，動遭齟齬，名雖愜於清論，事無益於人國，可慨也哉！雖然，數公之論諫固忠矣、直矣，而於所以論諫之道，亦容有不盡也。孔子曰：「勿欺也，而犯
translation_en:
…Zhu and Chen Maolian, implicated for criticizing the public-field policy, withdrew from office one after another. People of the time called them the Three Resolute Men, and countless voices spoke as one of their outspoken loyalty and integrity. How could they be ashamed beside the Three Secretariat Drafters? Other examples are those who, during the Qingyuan era, prostrated themselves at the palace gates and submitted a petition to clear Zhao Ruyu of the injustice done him: Yang Hongzhong, Zhou Duanchao, Zhang Dao, Lin Zhonglin, Jiang Fu, and Xu Fan. Although they were banished five hundred li away, their reputation as the Six Gentlemen spread throughout the court and the realm. Were they seeking praise from others? Their words indeed contributed to the affairs of their age. Those who, during the Baoyou era, prostrated themselves at the palace doors to present their case and impeach Ding Daquan for his villainy were Chen Yizhong, Huang Yong, Lin Zezu, Zeng Wei, Liu Fu, and Chen Zong. Although they were placed under supervised residence in distant prefectures, their designation as the Six Gentlemen spread far and wide. Were they angling for fame among the multitude? Their words indeed bore directly upon the government of the time [?].

A heart of loyalty and righteousness gives rise to words of uncompromising candor. In the remonstrances of these gentlemen, the matters differed, but all sprang from loyalty and righteousness; their views varied, but all tended toward forthright integrity. Their loyal hearts were like the blazing sun, their unyielding spirit like autumn frost. Had they won their rulers’ confidence and put their proposals into practice, they surely would have done much to correct faults, remedy failings, and improve government. Yet their Way ran counter to their times, and at every turn they encountered obstruction. Though their reputations won the approval of impartial opinion, their actions brought no benefit to their rulers’ states. How lamentable!
