title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之子夏曰君子信而後諫觀夫虞周之時
臯稷陳謨周召進戒格心之學優游浸漬
引其君於當道措其民於泰和上以成君
之明下不顯己之直何者不欺之誠一念
之信有以孚之於素也豈至臨事犯顏自
取斥辱章君之闕而徒擅一身之名哉方
今
聖天子在上
駿德格天忠賢布列廟堂有都俞之風天下有
===
雍熈之化固無事於言矣然明問俯及乃
欲扣異日得言之志顧愚草茅賤士何所
知哉但所謂今事之當先則輾轉胸中千
慮一得固有如數公之所言者所謂古人
之當法則臯稷周召乃所願焉而姑置乎
數公矣脫不棄而與進之尚當瀝葵藿之
誠而敷獻于
玉墀之下謹對
第五問
punctuated:
之。子夏曰：「君子信而後諫。」觀夫虞周之時，臯稷陳謨，周召進戒，格心之學，優游浸漬，引其君於當道，措其民於泰和，上以成君之明，下不顯己之直。何者？不欺之誠，一念之信，有以孚之於素也。豈至臨事犯顏，自取斥辱，章君之闕，而徒擅一身之名哉？方今聖天子在上，駿德格天，忠賢布列，廟堂有都俞之風，天下有雍熈之化，固無事於言矣。然明問俯及，乃欲扣異日得言之志。顧愚草茅賤士，何所知哉？但所謂今事之當先，則輾轉胸中，千慮一得，固有如數公之所言者；所謂古人之當法，則臯稷周召乃所願焉，而姑置乎數公矣。脫不棄而與進之，尚當瀝葵藿之誠，而敷獻于玉墀之下。謹對。

第五問
translation_en:
… him. Zixia said: “The gentleman remonstrates only after he has gained trust.” Consider the ages of Yu and Zhou: Gao and Ji presented their counsels, and the Dukes of Zhou and Shao offered admonitions. Through their learning in rectifying the ruler’s heart, they influenced him gently and gradually, guiding their sovereign onto the proper way and settling his people in perfect harmony. Above, they perfected their ruler’s discernment; below, they did not display their own uprightness. Why was this? Their sincerity in never deceiving him and their steadfast good faith had already won his trust. How could they have come to the point of confronting his displeasure when affairs arose, bringing rejection and humiliation upon themselves, exposing their ruler’s failings, and merely securing a reputation for themselves?

Now the sagely Son of Heaven reigns above. His magnificent virtue reaches Heaven; loyal and worthy men fill the ranks. At court there prevails the spirit of approving assent found in antiquity, and throughout the realm there is the transforming influence of concord and prosperity. There is assuredly no need for remonstrance. Yet your discerning question has condescended to reach us, seeking to inquire into our intentions should we one day gain an opportunity to speak. But I am a foolish and humble scholar from the countryside: what could I know? As for what should take priority in present affairs, I have turned the matter over and over in my breast; among a thousand reflections, my one useful insight does indeed accord with what those several gentlemen said. As for which men of antiquity should serve as models, it is Gao, Ji, and the Dukes of Zhou and Shao whom I wish to emulate, setting those other gentlemen aside for the moment. If I am not cast aside but granted advancement, I shall pour out my devotion, like the sunflower and bean leaves turning toward the sun, and fully present it below the jade steps of the throne. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fifth Question

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
周澤
同考試官教諭俞批〔有考據斷制盖策塲之優者〕
同考試官教諭王批〔援古證今其達國計者歟〕
同考試官教諭劉批〔財用一策敷答詳盡可謂博古通今者矣〕
考試官學正陳批〔財用一策正欲觀士子學識此策條無遺宜寘前列〕
考試官教授黄批〔酌古今而得理財之宜鑿鑿乎有用之學也〕
===
財用制乎古而周官之法詳財用制於今
而地官之任重盖財者軍國之需不可不
理也其取用之制莫善於成周尤莫善於
我
朝也夫豈漢唐宋之所可及哉且財用關於
天下國家大矣尚清談者以會計為末務
事箕會者以苛斂為竒能而不知大學論
絜矩專以是為言者盖深探其本矣粤自
成周以冢宰而制國用如會同軍旅之需
punctuated:
周澤

同考試官教諭俞批〔有考據斷制，盖策塲之優者。〕
同考試官教諭王批〔援古證今，其達國計者歟！〕
同考試官教諭劉批〔財用一策，敷答詳盡，可謂博古通今者矣。〕
考試官學正陳批〔財用一策，正欲觀士子學識，此策條無遺，宜寘前列。〕
考試官教授黄批〔酌古今而得理財之宜，鑿鑿乎有用之學也。〕

財用制乎古，而周官之法詳；財用制於今，而地官之任重。盖財者，軍國之需，不可不理也。其取用之制，莫善於成周，尤莫善於我朝也，夫豈漢唐宋之所可及哉！且財用關於天下國家大矣，尚清談者以會計為末務，事箕會者以苛斂為竒能，而不知《大學》論絜矩，專以是為言者，盖深探其本矣。粤自成周，以冢宰而制國用，如會同軍旅之需
translation_en:
Zhou Ze

Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: 〔Supported by textual evidence and decisive judgments; surely an outstanding policy essay in this examination.〕
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔He invokes antiquity to substantiate his arguments about the present. Is he not someone who understands state finance?〕
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔His response to the policy question on finance is detailed and comprehensive. He may be called well versed in antiquity and thoroughly conversant with the present.〕
Examiner Chen, School Rector, comments: 〔The policy question on finance was intended precisely to reveal the candidates’ learning and understanding. This essay leaves no point untreated and should be ranked among the foremost.〕
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: 〔Weighing ancient and present practice, he arrives at appropriate methods of managing finance. This is assuredly learning of practical use.〕

Financial resources and expenditure were regulated in antiquity, and the methods in the Offices of Zhou were comprehensive; financial resources and expenditure are regulated today, and the responsibilities of the Minister of Revenue are weighty. Wealth supplies the needs of the military and the state and therefore must be managed. No system for collecting and using it surpassed that of the Zhou, and above all none surpasses that of our dynasty. How could the Han, Tang, or Song possibly match it? Moreover, finance is of immense consequence to the realm and the state. Those who esteem lofty discourse regard accounting as a minor concern; those occupied with fiscal calculations [?] regard oppressive exactions as exceptional ability. They fail to understand that when the Great Learning discusses the principle of the measuring square, its particular emphasis on this subject probes deeply into the roots of the matter. From the time of the Zhou, the Grand Steward regulated state expenditure, including the requirements of assemblies of the feudal lords and military campaigns …

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皆自外府給之而總其所出者冢宰也金
玉貨賄之珍皆於玉府藏之而總其所入
者亦冢宰也是以當時圜法流通泉布充
足而人主無侈用之心者豈非利拳之歸
於一乎惟其一則人不得以貳之此成周
之法為古人之善法也漢除秦弊以相國
而任會計其公藏則主於內史而總之者
相國也私藏則主於少府而領之者亦相
國也是以當時饋餉不乏陳腐相因而國
===
家有富庶之效者豈非利拳之任猶專於
一乎惟其專則人不得以分之此漢初之
法猶有成周之遺意也自平勃失對之後
遂以供養勞賜出於少府軍國大計歸於
司農而拳分為二矣孳牲蕃畜出於上林
水衡而拳裂為三矣是以西羌之役司農
不継而續以少府之禁錢降胡之費司農
不給而補以御府之禁錢周之意固如是
乎自相國拳移之後唐以度支郎掌歲計
punctuated: 皆自外府給之，而總其所出者，冢宰也。金玉貨賄之珍，皆於玉府藏之，而總其所入者，亦冢宰也。是以當時圜法流通，泉布充足，而人主無侈用之心者，豈非利拳之歸於一乎？惟其一，則人不得以貳之，此成周之法為古人之善法也。漢除秦弊，以相國而任會計。其公藏則主於內史，而總之者，相國也；私藏則主於少府，而領之者，亦相國也。是以當時饋餉不乏，陳腐相因，而國家有富庶之效者，豈非利拳之任猶專於一乎？惟其專，則人不得以分之，此漢初之法猶有成周之遺意也。自平勃失對之後，遂以供養勞賜出於少府，軍國大計歸於司農，而拳分為二矣；孳牲蕃畜出於上林水衡，而拳裂為三矣。是以西羌之役，司農不継，而續以少府之禁錢；降胡之費，司農不給，而補以御府之禁錢。周之意固如是乎？自相國拳移之後，唐以度支郎掌歲計
translation_en:
…were all supplied from the Outer Treasury, while the Minister of State oversaw all disbursements. Precious gold, jade, goods, and valuables were all stored in the Jade Treasury, and the Minister of State likewise oversaw all receipts. Thus, currency circulated freely, money was plentiful, and the ruler had no inclination toward extravagant expenditure. Was this not because financial authority [?; transcribed throughout as 拳] was concentrated in a single office? Precisely because it was unified, no one could establish a competing authority. This is why the institutions of the Zhou were exemplary institutions of antiquity.

The Han abolished the abuses of the Qin and entrusted fiscal accounting to the Chancellor of State. Its public treasury was administered by the Metropolitan Commandant, with the Chancellor of State exercising overall supervision; its private treasury was administered by the Chamberlain for Palace Revenues, likewise under the Chancellor of State’s direction. Thus military provisions never ran short, old grain accumulated until it spoiled, and the state attained wealth and abundance. Was this not because responsibility for financial authority remained concentrated in a single office? Precisely because it was concentrated, no one could divide it. In this respect, the institutions of the early Han still preserved the underlying intention of the Zhou.

After Chen Ping and Zhou Bo failed to give an answer [?], expenditure for the ruler’s maintenance and for rewards came to be supplied by the Chamberlain for Palace Revenues, while the principal military and state finances fell to the Chamberlain for the National Treasury: authority was thus divided in two. The breeding and raising of livestock fell to the Chief Commandant of Waters and Parks at Shanglin, and authority was thereby split in three. Consequently, during the campaign against the Western Qiang, when the Chamberlain for the National Treasury could not sustain the expenditure, the shortfall was met from the privy funds of the Chamberlain for Palace Revenues. When the Chamberlain for the National Treasury could not meet the expenses of the surrendered Hu, the deficit was made up from the privy funds of the Imperial Treasury. Was this really the intention of the Zhou?

After authority shifted away from the Chancellor of State, the Tang placed the Director of the Bureau of Revenue in charge of the annual accounts…

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之所出復有判專判諸郎之設而隨設
隨罷焉後唐以户部掌財計之所會復有
度支鹽鐵三司之立而屢變屢分焉周之
制固如此乎宋以三司而寓冢宰之任造
作軍器屬之冑案土木之役屬之脩造河
防之役屬之河渠而三司則制其所出也
轉運督財賦之集内庭貯錢帛之私而三
司則統其所入也其與冢宰總外府王府
之意同乎夫古者井田之法立而富藏於
===
民阡陌之法行而富藏於國鹽鐵之使立
則富藏於府庫矣且酤之有禁為傷德也
而漢唐則榷之似矣茶之為物則草食也
而唐宋亦榷之可乎禹貢之青州貢鹽民
之利廣也而歷代榷之似矣周官之楮幣
貿易民之利微也而歷代亦取之可乎嗟
夫法無古今便民者良洪惟我
國家損益歷代参酌時宜闢自古所無之土
地統自古未有之人民鹽則藏於民而禁
punctuated: 之所出，復有判專判諸郎之設，而隨設隨罷焉。後唐以户部掌財計之所會，復有度支鹽鐵三司之立，而屢變屢分焉。周之制固如此乎？宋以三司而寓冢宰之任，造作軍器屬之冑案，土木之役屬之脩造，河防之役屬之河渠，而三司則制其所出也。轉運督財賦之集，内庭貯錢帛之私，而三司則統其所入也。其與冢宰總外府王府之意同乎？夫古者井田之法立，而富藏於民；阡陌之法行，而富藏於國；鹽鐵之使立，則富藏於府庫矣。且酤之有禁，為傷德也，而漢唐則榷之，似矣；茶之為物，則草食也，而唐宋亦榷之，可乎？《禹貢》之青州貢鹽，民之利廣也，而歷代榷之，似矣；《周官》之楮幣貿易，民之利微也，而歷代亦取之，可乎？嗟夫！法無古今，便民者良。洪惟我國家，損益歷代，参酌時宜，闢自古所無之土地，統自古未有之人民。鹽則藏於民而禁
translation_en:
…the expenditures, and further established various posts of directors and specialist directors [?], only to abolish them as soon as they were established. Under the Later Tang, the Ministry of Revenue handled the consolidation of financial accounts; yet the Three Fiscal Commissions—Revenue, Expenditure, and Salt and Iron—were also established, repeatedly reorganized and divided. Was this really the system of the Zhou?

The Song vested the responsibilities of the Grand Steward in the Three Fiscal Commissions. The manufacture of military equipment belonged to the Armor Section, building works to the Construction Section, and river-defense works to the Waterways Section; the Three Fiscal Commissions controlled their expenditures. The Transport Commissioners supervised the collection of tax revenues, while the inner court stored its private reserves of money and silk; the Three Fiscal Commissions oversaw their receipts. Was the intent here the same as that of placing the Outer Treasury and Royal Treasury under the Grand Steward?

In antiquity, when the well-field system was established, wealth was stored among the people. When the system of fields divided by boundary paths came into practice, wealth was stored in the state. When commissioners for salt and iron were established, wealth came to be stored in government treasuries. Restrictions on selling liquor existed because it injured virtue, so the Han and Tang monopolies on it seem reasonable. But tea is a plant consumed as food: was it acceptable for the Tang and Song to monopolize it too? In the Tribute of Yu, Qingzhou presented salt as tribute. The profits it afforded the people were extensive, so monopolizing it under successive dynasties seems reasonable. But the paper currency used in trade in the Offices of Zhou [?] afforded the people only slight profits: was it acceptable for successive dynasties to take these too?

Alas! Laws need not be judged by whether they are ancient or modern: those that benefit the people are good. We reverently reflect that our great dynasty has adapted the institutions of successive dynasties, weighing the needs of the times. It has opened up territory on a scale unprecedented since antiquity and governs a population likewise without precedent. Salt remains in the hands of the people, yet restrictions are imposed…

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之者恐其亂公法耳茶則採於民而禁之
者恐其交外夷耳酤則造於民而弛其禁
幣則造於官而便乎民方今財賦重於東
南而尤重於江浙天下視之以為盈縮也
故漕運之設舟楫往來而饋餉賴之以給
課鹽之地商賈輻輳而邊需賴之以充而
其坑冶之所出不過助不及焉耳
朝廷節用愛人無所不至猶慮豐歉相承而
耗衍倚伏故專任戶部以會計之此萬古
===
不易之法也然當益重其任務在得人又
必如大學絜矩之道務本以豐其源節用
以防其流則生財有道取用有節
國用以之而足民力以之而紓雖成周之制
不過是也或謂大臣不當理財賦夫豈知
本之論哉
punctuated: 之者，恐其亂公法耳。茶則採於民，而禁之者，恐其交外夷耳。酤則造於民，而弛其禁；幣則造於官，而便乎民。方今財賦重於東南，而尤重於江浙，天下視之以為盈縮也。故漕運之設，舟楫往來，而饋餉賴之以給；課鹽之地，商賈輻輳，而邊需賴之以充。而其坑冶之所出，不過助不及焉耳。朝廷節用愛人，無所不至，猶慮豐歉相承，而耗衍倚伏，故專任戶部以會計之。此萬古不易之法也。然當益重其任，務在得人，又必如《大學》絜矩之道，務本以豐其源，節用以防其流，則生財有道，取用有節，國用以之而足，民力以之而紓。雖成周之制，不過是也。或謂大臣不當理財賦，夫豈知本之論哉！
translation_en:
…the reason for restricting it is simply the fear that it might disrupt public law. Tea is gathered by the people, and restrictions upon it arise simply from concern over dealings with foreign peoples. Alcohol is produced by the people, and restrictions upon it have been relaxed; currency is produced by the government for the convenience of the people. At present, the burden of taxation falls heavily upon the southeast, and especially upon Jiangsu and Zhejiang; the empire looks to these regions to determine whether its resources will be abundant or deficient. Thus, under the grain transport system, boats ply back and forth, and the provision of supplies depends upon them. In the areas where salt duties are levied, merchants converge like spokes upon a hub, and frontier requirements depend upon these revenues for their fulfillment. The proceeds from mining and smelting merely help make up shortfalls.

The court practices economy and cares for the people in every possible way. Yet it remains concerned that plentiful and lean years succeed one another, and that depletion and surplus lie latent within each other. It therefore assigns particular responsibility to the Ministry of Revenue to account for these resources. This is a principle that will remain unchanged for all ages. Nevertheless, greater weight should be given to this responsibility, with the essential task being to find suitable men. Moreover, one must follow the Way of the measuring square taught in the Great Learning: attend to the fundamentals to replenish the sources of wealth, and economize on expenditure to restrain its outflow. Then wealth will be produced in accordance with the proper Way, and its collection and use will be regulated. State expenditures will thereby be adequately supplied, and the burdens upon the people’s resources and labor will be eased. Even the institutions of the perfected Zhou order went no further than this. Some say that high ministers ought not to manage taxation and revenue. How could such an argument show any understanding of the fundamentals?

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
浙士中試者九十人合九十
人三試之文而拔其尤彰明
者為是録諸士子平日明於
心習於身脩於家以待用天
下者盡著于此舉而措之焉
往不濟切聞聖人惡文之過
===
質君子耻言之違行記誦涉
獵以幸一得又科目之通患
此先正所以病其妨正學也
使能實知於心允踐于身刑
成於家其達也有施其窮也
有守而富貴利禄一不以先
後得失少動於中是即古賓
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

浙士中試者九十人。合九十人三試之文，而拔其尤彰明者，為是録。諸士子平日明於心、習於身、脩於家，以待用天下者，盡著于此。舉而措之，焉往不濟？切聞聖人惡文之過質，君子耻言之違行。記誦涉獵，以幸一得，又科目之通患。此先正所以病其妨正學也。使能實知於心，允踐于身，刑成於家，其達也有施，其窮也有守，而富貴利禄一不以先後得失少動於中，是即古賓
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

Ninety scholars from Zhejiang passed the examination. Their writings from all three sessions were brought together, and the most outstanding and lucid were selected to form this record. Everything these scholars have habitually understood in their minds, practiced in their persons, and cultivated within their families, in preparation for service in the world, is fully displayed here. If they put these things into practice, where could they fail to accomplish something?

I have heard that the sage abhors literary refinement exceeding substance, and that the gentleman is ashamed when his words diverge from his deeds. Relying on memorization and miscellaneous reading in hopes of a lucky success is also a common failing of the examination system. This is why earlier worthies deplored its interference with true learning. If these scholars can possess genuine understanding in their minds, faithfully practice it in their persons, and establish an exemplary pattern within their families, they will have something to put into effect when successful and something to hold fast to when in adversity. If wealth, rank, profit, and emoluments do not stir their hearts in the slightest, whether obtained sooner or later, gained or lost, then they are precisely those whom the ancients honored as guests …

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
興賢能庶常吉士也何所復
議哉今兩浙名藩士習素厚
去古人不遠諸士子尚克永
觀省以聖賢極致自期待無
失于前者當慎成于後未足
于往者當勉進于來沿于故
肄當有獨見之明逐于群趨
===
當有特立之勇他日治千古
義毋忘是錄之經書政切時
要毋忘是錄之論策知
制代言則所習詔誥之大體當謹
進章折獄則經試表判之正
言勿渝凡百猷為永惟初服
務使文與質宣言與行合名
punctuated: 興賢能、庶常吉士也，何所復議哉？今兩浙名藩，士習素厚，去古人不遠。諸士子尚克永觀省，以聖賢極致自期待。無失于前者，當慎成于後；未足于往者，當勉進于來。沿于故肄，當有獨見之明；逐于群趨，當有特立之勇。他日治千古義，毋忘是錄之經書；政切時要，毋忘是錄之論策。知制代言，則所習詔誥之大體當謹；進章折獄，則經試表判之正言勿渝。凡百猷為，永惟初服，務使文與質宣，言與行合，名
translation_en:
…the worthy and capable men advanced in antiquity, the fine scholars appointed to ordinary offices. What further objection could there be? Now the two Zhe regions constitute a distinguished province, where the habits of scholars have long been sound and remain close to those of the ancients. May you scholars continually reflect upon and examine yourselves, aspiring to the highest attainments of sages and worthies. Those who have committed no fault thus far should take care to bring their work to completion hereafter; those whose earlier efforts have fallen short should strive to advance in the future. When following established studies, possess the discernment to see for yourselves; when swept along with the crowd, possess the courage to stand independently.

When in days to come you study principles enduring through the ages, do not forget the treatment of the Classics in this record; when your administration addresses the pressing needs of the time, do not forget its discourses and policy essays. When drafting imperial commands and speaking on the ruler’s behalf, carefully observe the general principles of edicts and proclamations that you have studied. When submitting memorials or deciding legal cases, do not depart from the correct language of the memorials and legal judgments tested in the examination. In all your plans and actions, keep your initial commitment forever in mind. Strive to ensure that literary refinement and substance give expression to one another, that words accord with deeds, and that reputation…

title: 成化十九年浙江鄉試錄
text:
與實孚所謂上不負
天子下不負所學然後科目有光
鄉國增重是錄信可稱賢能
之書也今茲鹿鳴罷宴鴻漸
及時將與天下豪傑翺翔下
上于雲空之表非明輩所能
測識尚惟笙簧之音未絕干
===
磐之迹近存諸士子可遽泯
一日惠好而有遐心哉芻蕘
之言幸無相忘也
山東東昌府高唐州儒學學
正陳明謹序
punctuated:
與實孚，所謂上不負天子，下不負所學，然後科目有光，鄉國增重，是錄信可稱賢能之書也。今茲鹿鳴罷宴，鴻漸及時，將與天下豪傑翺翔下上于雲空之表，非明輩所能測識。尚惟笙簧之音未絕，干磐之迹近存，諸士子可遽泯一日惠好而有遐心哉？芻蕘之言，幸無相忘也。
山東東昌府高唐州儒學學正陳明謹序。
translation_en:
…and accord with reality. This is what is meant by not failing the Son of Heaven above or one’s own learning below. Only then will the examination system gain lustre and one’s native region acquire greater standing; this record may indeed be called a book of the worthy and capable. Now the Deer Cry banquet has ended, and the time has come for the wild geese to advance. You will soar with the outstanding men of the realm, rising and descending beyond the clouds, to heights that the likes of me, Ming, cannot fathom. Yet the notes of the reed organs have not ceased, and traces of the ceremonial shields and chimes [?] still linger nearby. Can you scholars so soon efface the kindness and friendship of this day and become distant at heart? These are the words of a humble grass-cutter and wood-gatherer; I hope you will not forget them.
Preface respectfully composed by Chen Ming, School Instructor of the Confucian School of Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong.
